aiia.concept.body: Download a .md file that summarizes everything the app can do. Give it to any AI (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Le Chat, Copilot, etc.) — it will be able to answer all your questions about MyKTAMap with precise, up-to-date context.
aiia.how.step1: Pick your topic below, then 📋 Copy the context (or 📥 Download)
aiia.how.step2: Open the AI of your choice (web, mobile app, etc.)
aiia.how.step3: Copy-paste the file into the first message of the conversation
aiia.how.step4: Ask your questions: "How do I add a point?", "My plan is crashing, what do I do?", etc.
aiia.note.body: Using an AI may be paid or limited depending on the service (free ChatGPT with quotas, Claude Pro, etc.). MyKTAMap stays free — the downloaded context is just to help an external AI answer you better.
aiia.privacy.body: The file contains only the app's documentation — no personal data (none of your plans, points, sessions, photos). If you tick "technical state", it additionally includes anonymous technical info (version, device, plan modes, latest errors) — never your plan names or map data.
aiia.prompt.intro: Paste this text together with the .md file in the AI's first message. It sets the rules and limits hallucinations.
aiia.prompt.text:
Here is the official context of the MyKTAMap application (attached .md file or text pasted below).

You will help me use it by following these STRICT rules:

⛔ Answer ONLY from the content of the provided context.
⛔ If a feature is not described in it, say so clearly — NEVER make things up.
⛔ Do not extrapolate from other apps (Google Maps, QGIS, etc.).
⛔ You have access neither to the source code, nor the website, nor my application.
✅ Cite the section of the context where you find the info (e.g. "According to the Route recipe…").
✅ Use the exact icons and labels mentioned in the doc, with concrete steps.
✅ Always answer in MY language.
✅ If a "🔧 Installation state" block is present at the end of the context, use it for troubleshooting.

If you have understood, simply reply "OK, ready" and wait for my first question.

config.display.intersections.hint: Filled colored circle where 2 paths cross (green × purple → yellow, etc.). Uncheck to declutter very dense maps, or if the computation slows down rendering. Immediate effect, saved per map (another map keeps its own setting).
config.display.intersections.label: ⚪ Show circles at intersections (this map)

config.display.scaledMarkers.hint: On by default: point icons shrink when you zoom out (constant size relative to the map). Uncheck = standard Leaflet behavior (fixed screen-size icons, they become huge when zoomed out). Reload required after changing.
config.display.scaledMarkers.label: 📐 Scale icon size with zoom
config.display.vibration.hint: A short vibration on confirmations (waypoint reached, action validated, alert). Unticking means complete silence, handy underground with others. iOS does not give this sensor to web pages: on iPhone the option shows, but greyed out. Emergency alerts (exit found, critical alert) always vibrate.
config.display.vibration.label: 📳 Haptic vibration
config.display.voice.hint: Control the app by voice: zoom, center, search, add point, tracker on/off, emergency/rescue mode, light/dark theme… Push-to-talk via a floating 🎤 button bottom-right. Say “help” out loud to list the available commands. Microphone permission requested on first use. Reload required after changing (to inject/remove the button).
config.display.voice.label: 🎤 Voice commands (BETA)
config.display.voice.toastOn: 🎤 Voice commands enabled. 🎤 button shown at bottom right.
config.display.wakelock.hint: Prevents the screen from sleeping while the app is open. Ideal underground so you don't have to unlock your phone every 30s. Persistent across sessions. The wake lock is auto-released when you switch tab/app, and re-enabled on return if the box is checked.
config.display.wakelock.label: 🔆 Keep screen on (Wake Lock)
config.display.wakelock.toastOn: 🔆 Screen kept on while the app is open
config.georef.clickFloater: Click on the map to set Point {letter}
config.georef.errAllRequired: All fields are required (map x/y + GPS for A and B).
config.georef.errInvalidGps: Invalid GPS coordinates — fix the fields in red.
config.georef.intro: Calibrate the map by entering 2 reference points (map x/y coordinates + WGS84 GPS lat/lng). MyKTAMap computes the rotation+scale+translation transform to project all annotations onto the globe. The calibration is saved locally per map and automatically pre-filled when you open 📡 External export (KMZ / GPX) or import a GPX.
config.georef.okSaved: ✅ Calibration saved. Auto-filled in 📡 External export.
config.georef.estimerTitle: Derive point B from A, the plan scale and its North orientation
config.georef.estimeBadge: Point B is ESTIMATED (derived from A + scale + North) — not a measurement. Check the OSM overlay.
config.georef.estimerErrA: Point A incomplete: fill in X, Y and the GPS coordinates of A first.
config.georef.estimerErrScale: Plan scale missing or invalid (px/m). The estimate relies entirely on it — calibrate it first.
config.georef.estimerErrDims: Image dimensions unknown — load the plan image first.
config.georef.estimerErrCalc: Estimation impossible with these values (latitude too polar or invalid data).
config.georef.estimerConfirm:
Point B will be ESTIMATED ~{dist} m from A, under 2 assumptions:
• reliable scale: {scale} px/m
• plan North orientation: {north}° ("Calibrate North" setting)

Any scale or orientation error will shift the OSM view, KMZ/GPX exports and Rescue Mode accordingly. Check the OSM overlay afterwards.

Continue?
config.georef.estimerOk: Point B estimated — remember to Save, then check the OSM view.
config.georef.pointCHint: Corrects a globally distorted map (stretched assembly, different X/Y scales). Pick a point FAR from the A-B line. Leave empty if your map already projects well.
config.georef.errCIncomplete: Point C is incomplete: fill its 4 fields (X, Y, GPS) or leave them all empty.
config.georef.errCColineaire: Point C is too aligned with A and B: pick a point far from the A-B line (otherwise it adds nothing).
config.georef.confirmClear:
Delete the georeferencing saved for this map?
Without it: no OSM View and no KMZ / GPX export, until 2 new GPS points are surveyed.
config.georef.etatNonCalibre: — Map not georeferenced (KMZ / GPX exports and OSM view unavailable)
config.incognito.confirmQuit:
Leave incognito mode?

All points/notes/tracker data accumulated in this window will be lost.
config.incognito.quit.desc:
Closes this incognito window. All accumulated data (points, tracker, notes) will be lost. Your main session stays intact in its own tab.
If the browser blocks the close, the tab automatically reloads in normal mode.
config.incognito.start.desc:
Opens a new window where no data is saved (no photos, no tracker, no preferences). Ideal for exploring a map in a public demo, lending your session to someone, or testing without polluting your local history. A visible purple border + a title badge remind you of the context.
On reload: everything is gone.

config.jonction.hint: After OK, click on the map to place the junction's points (as many as you want). The path will be dashed magenta and stay visible regardless of the active level.
config.jonction.intro: This junction (stairs, steep slope, internal shaft) links two levels.
config.niveaux.active.hint: All new elements (paths, points, zones, repositioned tracker) will be tagged with this level.
config.niveaux.controlTitle: Active level — click to change / filter
config.niveaux.visible.hint: Check the levels you want to show on the map. Junctions are visible if at least one of their endpoints touches a checked level.
config.niveaux.warn: ⚠️ Changing the active level cancels any path in progress and resets the visible filter to [active].
config.north.statusCalibrated: ✅ North calibrated at {deg}° from the top of the map (clockwise).
config.north.statusDefault: ℹ️ North = top of the map (default configuration).
config.perfultra.animOff.hint: Instant pan/zoom instead of animated. Reload required after changing.
config.perfultra.animOff.label: ⚡ Disable zoom/pan animations
config.perfultra.decim.hint: Simplifies polylines via Ramer-Douglas-Peucker. Paths look less smooth when zoomed out but render much faster.
config.perfultra.decim.label: 🪜 Decimate paths when zooming out
config.perfultra.intro: For large maps / weak devices. Enable 🚀 ULTRA to apply all optimizations at once, or tweak each lever individually. Changes apply on the fly — except options marked with an orange border, which require reloading the map to take effect.
config.perfultra.mobileZoomLimit.hint: Checked by default. On smartphones, caps the maximum zoom-out to avoid an OOM crash when Leaflet tries to render the whole image at minZoom. Unchecking allows the same max zoom-out as on PC (useful for an overview) but risks crashing on large maps. Reload required after changing.
config.perfultra.mobileZoomLimit.label: 🛡️ Limit zoom-out on mobile (memory crash guard)
config.perfultra.noIntersect.hint: Threshold lowered to 50 routes (vs 200 normally). No circles at crossroads beyond that.
config.perfultra.noIntersect.label: 🎯 Disable intersection circles (large maps)
config.perfultra.noTooltips.hint: No more popup when clicking markers on data layers. Session points stay interactive. Use 🔍 to interact.
config.perfultra.noTooltips.label: 🚫 Disable popups on data layers
config.perfultra.slowSave.hint: Auto-save every 30s instead of 1.5s. Risk of losing ~30s of changes on a crash.
config.perfultra.slowSave.label: 🐢 Slow auto-save (30s)
config.perfultra.ultra.hint: Preset that enables the 7 toggles below. Unchecking disables everything.
config.perfultra.ultra.label: 🚀 ULTRA mode (enables everything)
config.perfultra.viewportCull.hint: Skips routes AND POI markers outside the viewport. Slight pop-in when panning but a huge gain on dense maps (100+ POI).
config.perfultra.viewportCull.label: 👁️ Render only visible elements
config.perfultra.tousNiveaux.hint: Unchecked: only levels -1, 0 and +1 show at opening. Applied at the next map load.
config.perfultra.tousNiveaux.label: 🏗️ Show every level at launch
config.presentation.desc: Hides the header + sidebars + footer to free up the whole surface for the map. Exit: <kbd>F</kbd> or <kbd>Esc</kbd> (PC), or the floating ✕ button top-right (mobile).
config.smartnav.hint: The tracker snaps to the nearest gallery instead of drifting beside it. Setting specific to THIS plan — it depends on how well this one is traced, and means nothing on a plan without paths.
config.smartnav.label: 🧭 Snap position to paths (this plan)
config.smartnav.headingHint: Penalty for heading misalignment at junctions (default 0.7). Lower it to pass junctions more easily even when misaligned; 0 = heading no longer used.
config.snapdraw.label: 🧲 Snap while drawing
config.snapdraw.hint: While drawing a path, a click near an existing point snaps exactly onto it. Your galleries truly meet instead of nearly touching — routes get through better. A golden flash confirms the snap. Only affects what you draw from now on.
config.snapdraw.radiusHint: On-screen distance under which snapping happens (default 14). Measured on screen, so it behaves the same at every zoom level. Raise it if snapping feels too rare.
config.smartnav.radiusHint: Max distance from the trace before decoupling (default 6). Increase if you decouple too easily.
config.smartnav.warn: ⚠️ Expert settings. A wrong value can degrade or completely break tracking. If something goes wrong: restore the defaults (6 and 0.7) or reset the settings.
config.smartnav.toastOff: 🧭 Smart navigation disabled for this map
config.smartnav.toastOn: 🧭 Smart navigation enabled for this map

export.full.anonymizeHint:
Replaces names with codes (💎 POI #1, 🛣️ Path #1, ⬛ Zone #1…), clears descriptions/notes, removes GPS history and profile. Coordinates, tags and map structure preserved — usable by anyone who knows the area.
📸 Photos can be included: each photo is re-encoded without metadata (EXIF/GPS stripped). The free note and History PDF remain excluded.

export.full.photosHint: If checked AND at least 1 photo: the export will be a .zip containing session.json + photos/. If unchecked OR 0 photo: a standard .json export.

export.kmz.niveauxHint: Default: all available levels (1 KML Folder per level).

home.netdoc.lead: MyKTAMap is a 100% client-side PWA. Everything you create (annotations, sessions, saved maps, KMZ calibrations, preferences) stays in your browser. The Nginx server only serves static files. No application backend, no server database, no analytics, no tracking cookie.
home.netdoc.quote: « If you find anything that contradicts this page, contact me (Instagram @karma_kta or contact@myktamap.fr) — I will fix it immediately. »
home.netdoc.scope1: This security and no-telemetry guarantee applies ONLY to the official domain myktamap.fr (and to the development environment dev.myktamap.fr, run by the same author).
home.netdoc.scope2: MyKTAMap's source code is public (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) and can be copied, forked or mirrored by anyone. Any third-party install — whatever name or domain it uses, even one claiming to be « MyKTAMap » — may contain modifications we are not responsible for: added tracking, data exfiltration, injected malicious code. We have no way to verify what goes on there.
home.netdoc.scope3: How to make sure you are on the real site? Check the URL in your browser's address bar. If it does not start with https://myktamap.fr or https://dev.myktamap.fr, nothing written on this page concerns you — it is a copy we have no control over.
home.netdoc.title: 📖 What does the app do on the network?
home.netdoc.verify1: Internal log: the « 📋 View the network log » button in the same section — logs in real time every request the app emits.
home.netdoc.verify2: Browser DevTools (F12): « Network » tab → you see every request, regardless of what the app claims. Filter by method to confirm there is no POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE.
home.netdoc.verify3: Strict offline mode: tick the toggle in the same section. The browser will actively refuse any non-whitelisted request — the app stays 100% functional.
home.netdoc.verify4: Content Security Policy: F12 → Network → first request (HTML) → Headers tab → look for Content-Security-Policy. The Nginx server tells the browser to block any non-whitelisted connection (connect-src 'self' https://www.gstatic.com).

Closes this incognito window. All accumulated data (points, tracker, notes) will be lost. Your main session stays intact in its tab.

Opens a new window where no data is saved (no photos, no tracker, no preferences). Ideal for exploring a map in a public demo, lending your session to someone else, or testing without polluting your local history. A purple border + a badge in the title are reminders of the context.

lost.tips.attendre.1: Settle in an identifiable spot (numbered shaft, named chamber, visible marking).
lost.tips.attendre.2: Stay where you are if nobody knows you're there — moving makes things worse.
lost.tips.attendre.3: Mark your location (paint, tape, a bright bag) so you can be found.
lost.tips.calme.1: Stop. Breathe in. Sit down for a few seconds.
lost.tips.calme.2: Panic makes you lose your bearings and wastes light + energy.
lost.tips.calme.3: Eat/drink a little if you have something. Catch your breath.
lost.tips.comm.1: If you get a signal (often near shafts / under certain manholes) → tell someone on the surface BEFORE your battery dies.
lost.tips.comm.2: The 📋 Copy report button below prepares a ready-made message with your last position + elapsed time.
lost.tips.lumiere.1: Switch your lamp to economy mode. Dead lamp = serious situation.
lost.tips.lumiere.2: Keep a backup lamp if you have one (headlamp + pen light is ideal).
lost.tips.lumiere.3: Hydrate a little but ration it — stress dehydrates you fast.
lost.tips.nepas.1: Don't follow the water — fissures often lead to dangerous narrow passages.
lost.tips.nepas.2: Don't attempt an unknown passage just because it seems to go up / head "toward the outside".
lost.tips.nepas.3: Don't trust the phone tracker — it drifts, especially under stress (erratic movements).
lost.tips.orient.1: Retrace your steps rather than trying to reach your destination — statistically more reliable.
lost.tips.orient.2: Look for the main axes (main galleries, straight galleries, railway tracks). They almost always lead to a known landmark.
lost.tips.orient.3: Use a physical compass — not the phone's, distorted by the ground and metal framework. Re-orient yourself at every junction.
lost.tips.orient.4: Listen to the sounds: traffic, subway, train, running water = useful directional clue.

oom.kill.intro: Last time, the app shut down abruptly and couldn't save its session normally.
oom.kill.tip.closeApps: Close other background apps before using MyKTAMap. On iPhone: double-tap Home or swipe up + dismiss the cards. On Android: multitask button + swipe away.
oom.kill.tip.export: Export your session regularly (📤 Export) so you lose nothing in case of an abrupt shutdown.
oom.kill.tip.optimize: If the problem persists on a specific map, its main image may be too large — it then needs re-optimizing (PNG compression or smaller dimensions).
oom.kill.tip.perf: Lower the performance mode in the loader (🚀 icon or via ⚙️ Settings). "Performance" loads smaller tiles and uses less RAM than "Quality".
oom.kill.tip.tabs: Avoid opening multiple browser tabs at once if you use the app via Safari/Chrome — each tab also uses memory.
oom.kill.tip.update: Keep your smartphone up to date: iOS and Android regularly improve their memory management for PWAs.
oom.kill.whyBody: On smartphones (iOS and Android), the operating system silently kills tabs and installed apps that use too much RAM. That's very often what happened here, especially if you're using a high-resolution map or many other apps were running at the same time.
oom.v2.explain: It's very likely a browser memory overload — V2 conversion decodes the source image at full resolution then generates N tiles, which can exceed the memory cap of mobile browsers (~500 MB on iOS Safari, variable on Android).
oom.v2.intro: Last time, you were running the V2 conversion of map {nom} (image {taille}) and the app shut down abruptly before it finished.
oom.v2.sol.closeApps: Close other apps in the background to free up RAM before retrying.
oom.v2.sol.pc: Do the conversion on a PC (Windows / macOS / Linux). No memory cap in practice. Once the V2 ZIP is generated, import it on your phone — the import is lightweight (no full-resolution decoding).
oom.v2.sol.resize: Shrink the source image to 6000-8000 px max before retrying (GIMP / Photoshop / Squoosh).

tutorial.card01.texte:
MyKTAMap is an underground mapping application built for the field: quarries, catacomb galleries, underground and industrial sites.

You work on a plan image (scanned paper map, drawing, photo). No GPS needed, no network needed — the app runs fully offline once loaded.

📜 License: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 — non-commercial use, share-alike. The code is public on GitHub (Karmakta91/MyKTAMap). This guarantee applies ONLY to the official domain myktamap.fr.

This short tour helps you discover the app in a few minutes. You can skip it at any time and replay it via 📖 Documentation → 🎓 button in the modal header.
tutorial.card01.hint: Navigate with the ◂ ▸ arrows or the ← → / Space keys on your keyboard.
tutorial.card02.texte:
MyKTAMap is a strictly client-side PWA:

  • ❌ No backend server, no remote database
  • ❌ No tracking cookies, no telemetry, no analytics
  • ❌ No account, no authentication, no cloud sync
  • ✅ Your annotations, sessions, plans and favorites stay locally in your browser (local storage + your browser’s local storage)
  • ✅ Only requests sent: same-origin (app assets) and a gstatic.com/generate_204 ping to detect connectivity

🔒 Check it yourself: open ⚙️ Configuration → 🔒 Network audit to see the LIVE log of every request the app sends. Also enable "Strict offline mode" which blocks any non-whitelisted request directly in the browser.

📜 Server-side CSP header (Nginx): connect-src 'self' https://www.gstatic.com — your browser ITSELF would refuse any exfiltration to an external domain, even if an attacker injected malicious JS.
tutorial.card03.texte:
From the home page, several ways to load an already available plan:

  • 📚 My plans: list of every plan you have already imported or created. Persisted in your browser’s local storage → you find them again on next launch without re-dropping anything.
  • 📦 Drop MyKTAMap ZIP: drop a .zip file in the drop zone. This is the native format — direct loading, full roundtrip (tags, levels, photos, custom legend preserved).
  • 📥 Drop KMZ / GPX: the same drop zone also accepts .kmz files (Google Earth, OsmAnd) and .gpx (TopoDroid, Strava, Garmin). The app automatically converts them into a rebuilt MyKTAMap ZIP.
  • 🌐 Server auto-discovery: if the app is installed on a server that exposes data/index.json, public plans are listed there automatically.

💡 Imported KMZ / GPX: ideally exported from MyKTAMap (100% preserved roundtrip). Otherwise, info missing from the standard format (MyKTAMap tags, M-LVL levels, etc.) is replaced by defaults. For a GPX with no image, the app generates a blank canvas auto-calibrated on the file's GPS bounds.
tutorial.card04.texte:
Want to start a new plan? Click 🏗️ Generate a plan on the home page. Simple Mode is the default option on first launch.

You get a ready-to-use MyKTAMap ZIP in 30 seconds with just:

  • 🖼️ A plan image (scan, photo, drawing) or a blank canvas (4 standard sizes + 4 color choices: sepia / white / grey / black)
  • 🏷️ A name and a version (the rest is auto-filled)
  • 🏗️ Optional: 🏗️ Multi-level plan checkbox for a multi-storey quarry
  • 🧱 Optional: 🧱 V2 tiled checkbox if plan ≥ 4000×4000 px (recommended for mobile perf)

Built-in icons (shafts, rooms, crawlways, hazards…) are auto-loaded. No need to touch data layers, tracking or GPS calibration — the app provides sensible default values.
tutorial.card04.hint: To switch to Advanced Mode: the "🎨 Advanced" button at the top of the generator.
tutorial.card05.texte:
The generator's Advanced Mode gives you full control over every technical parameter of the plan:

  • 🖼️ Image layers: stack several PNGs (e.g. raw plan + legend + scanned paper annotations) with configurable order and visibility
  • 📊 Data layers: embed point/path/zone/structure JSON files into the plan (e.g. shafts.json, vehicles.json). Read-only at runtime, filterable by layer in the map's Layers modal.
  • 🚶 Tracking configuration: tracker start position, px↔m scale, step length, threshold, cooldown
  • 🎨 Custom icons: replace the default icons, add 50×50 PNGs for new tags
  • 🌐 GPS georeferencing: 2 points (plan ↔ GPS) that enable KMZ/GPX export and GPS coordinates display in popups
  • 🏷️ Plan-level legend: customize labels + masks + custom entries embedded IN the plan ZIP (= cross-user sharing)

If you edit an existing plan (drop ZIP in the generator → Edit mode), the form is pre-filled with current values and automatically forces Advanced Mode.
tutorial.card06.titre: Turning a GIS survey into a plan
tutorial.card06.texte:
Home page → drop your file on the “📦 Load a new plan” area — the same one as for ZIPs. The conversion panel opens by itself.

Accepted formats: .geojson, .json, .kml, vector .kmz — what QGIS and survey software produce.

  • 🖼️ No image needed: a blank background is generated and aligned on the file’s coordinates by itself
  • 🏷️ Mapping screen: you say what each value in your file means — gallery, zone, pillar, quarry face. An object’s shape does not say what it is; you decide
  • 🏔️ One level per floor: pick the column carrying the level, and tick “one colour per level” — without it, six stacked floors blend together
  • 📐 Lambert 93 converted automatically (the French system, in metres). Other projections are refused: re-export as EPSG:4326 from QGIS

⚠️ A whole county survey is refused, on purpose: a MyKTAMap plan is one quarry, not a county. Cut it up first.

🔄 Once the plan is open you can still fix the survey: 🔍 Filters → Edit pulls the layer into your session, and a quarry face that is really a gallery is reclassified in one click.
tutorial.card06.hint: Routing only runs on paths: if your whole survey landed as structures, reclassify whatever is really a gallery.
tutorial.card07.texte:
Right sidebar → ✏️ (direct click = enables add mode)

Click the ✏️ icon to start add mode (the button gets highlighted). Then each click on the map drops a new marker. Click ✏️ again to exit the mode. A modal opens for each point with:

  • Name (= unique identifier, used by exports and the pathfinder)
  • Tags: typed icon among the built-ins (ventilation shaft, room, crawlway, passage, hazard, electricity…) or your plan's custom tags
  • State: not inspected / OK / dangerous (tints the icon)
  • Description multiline: free textarea, shown in the popup + embedded in KMZ / GPX / JSON exports
  • 📸 POI photos: up to 5 photos per point. Compressed locally (canvas → JPEG q85 max 1920px), stored in your browser’s local storage. Never sent to the Internet.

A point's popup (click on the marker):

  • 🌐 GPS coordinates if plan is calibrated — copyable to clipboard in one click
  • 📸 Photo thumbnails clickable → fullscreen viewer (pinch-zoom, swipe)
  • 🗺️ Go there: starts a route from your position to this point
  • ⭐ Favorite: marks this point as important
  • ✏️ Edit / 🗑️ Delete
tutorial.card08.texte:
Right sidebar → 🛣️ Paths → Main / Secondary / Trail

Click-click on the map to draw a polyline. Click the active icon again to validate the path. 3 predefined types with distinct colors:

  • 🟩 Main: large known galleries, main axes
  • 🟪 Secondary: junction galleries, less frequented
  • 🟨 Trail: narrow passages, shortcuts, exploratory paths

Paths are used by the pathfinder (Dijkstra) to compute automatic routes between 2 points (see card 16). Intersections are detected automatically (colored circles at crossings — color of the lowest-priority path).

💬 Note on a path: button in the popup → multiline textarea, embedded in exports. Ideal to annotate a gallery (state, hazards, landmarks).

📏 Path distance: visible in 📊 Session details, or via the 📏 Total distance tool (cumulative magenta highlight).
tutorial.card09.texte:
Right sidebar → ⬛ Zones → Water / Rubble / Collapse / Inaccessible

Click on the map to place the vertices of a polygon. Click the 1st vertex again to close the zone. 4 predefined types:

  • 💧 Water: puddle, lake, flooded area (blue)
  • ⬛ Rubble: scree, partial blockage, debris (grey)
  • 🟥 Collapse: dangerous area, fallen vault (red)
  • ⛔ Inaccessible: physically unreachable or forbidden area (red/black 45° hatching)

⚠️ Inaccessible zone — pathfinder effect: these zones BLOCK route computation. The pathfinder will refuse any path segment crossing an inaccessible zone. Even at the current active level in multi-level mode (inter-level junctions pass over without being blocked — vertical transit points). Since v1.82.0 you can release this constraint: a “Respect inaccessible zones” checkbox in the Route window, ticked by default. Unticking it lets the route cross them — an explicit choice, for someone who knows their ground. ⚠️ Rescue Mode and “Lost” always respect them: a convenience preference does not widen a rescue perimeter.

💬 Note on a zone: popup → textarea. Embedded in exports.
tutorial.card10.texte:
Right sidebar → 🏛️ Structures

Cataphile structures are the built / carved elements of the quarry. 5 predefined sub-types:

  • 🟡 Pillar (upper mass) (polygon): upper support pillar
  • 🟠 Pillar (lower mass) (polygon): lower pillar
  • 🔵 Wall (polygon): retaining wall, rubble barrier
  • 🟨 Working face (upper) (open line): extraction limit
  • 🟧 Working face (lower) (open line)

Polygon vs polyline difference:

  • Pillars + Wall = closed polygons (≥ 3 vertices) with fill color
  • Faces = open polylines (≥ 2 vertices) without fill

💬 Note on a structure: popup → textarea. Embedded in exports.

📊 Count stats: visible in 📊 Session details with breakdown by type.
tutorial.card11.texte:
You can customize the legend: rename types, hide the ones you don't use, or even add your own drawable types.

🎯 3-level cascade:

  1. Session: edits made from the map (🗺️ Legend modal → ✏️ Edit). Persisted locally with the current session.
  2. Plan: edits made from the Advanced Mode generator. Embedded IN the plan ZIP → shared with all users of this plan.
  3. MyKTAMap default: built-in values (Main, Water, Upper-mass pillar, etc.)

📋 Usage examples:

  • Rename "Water" → "Bottom lake" for YOUR plan
  • Hide "Lower-mass pillar" if the quarry has none
  • Add a new "⚠️ Toxic gas" type (red hatched polygon) to flag specific areas

🌍 KMZ + GPX roundtrip: the plan's custom legend travels with exports and is restored on re-import → even a recipient who opens your KMZ/GPX in MyKTAMap will find your renamings and your custom types.
tutorial.card12.texte:
The 🧭 Tracker mode (full-screen menu, right bar) uses your phone's motion sensors (accelerometer, magnetometer) to estimate your position in real time — without GPS (= useful underground).

Tracker menu tiles:

  • ▶️ Play / Stop: starts pedometer (Pedestrian Dead Reckoning) step detection. The marker moves according to your orientation and detected steps.
  • 🧭 Compass: rotating visual widget that counter-rotates to keep North up. Lets you verify the heading is correct.
  • 📍 Recalibrate: click on the map to teleport the marker to where you actually are. Use it every ~50 m to correct cumulative drift.
  • 🗺️ Route: opens the modal to compute a route from your current position.
  • 🎬 Replay: review your tracking session afterwards. Timeline slider + play/pause + speed 0.5× to 10× + CSV export of timestamped positions.
  • 🔥 Heatmap: cumulative multi-session foot-traffic density (see card 19).

⚠️ EXPERIMENTAL: drift is unavoidable (imprecise sensors + metal structures that throw off the magnetometer). It's a debug/curiosity tool, NOT a backup GPS. To locate yourself in a tense situation, use the ⛑️ I'm lost mode (next card).
tutorial.card13.texte:
3 complementary modes, at the bottom of the Tracker menu with a distinctive red background:

  • ⛑️ I'm lost: you roughly know where you've been but not where you are now. The app computes a probable area (search circle) from your last known position + elapsed time + estimated average speed. You can refine it by adding visual clues ("I saw a big red plaque", "there was a pillar here").
  • 🚨 XL emergency mode (panic): you know where you are (the tracker shows it) but you're panicking and need vital info BIG. Displays your GPS coordinates + compass heading + battery level fullscreen, hiding the rest of the UI. Saves your battery.
  • 🚨 Emergency exit: you want to get out fast. The app computes via pathfinder the optimal route from your position to the nearest exit — a surface-access POI (open cavage, shaft or stairway: tags cao / peo / eso) or tagged entrée (you can leave the way you came in). Shows distance + ETA + drawn route. Ideal when the battery is dropping, the tide is rising, or a storm is approaching above.

💡 3 different use cases:

  • ⛑️ = I do NOT know where I am → compute a search area
  • 🚨 panic = I know where I am → XL display to communicate the position
  • 🚨 exit = I know where I am → guides me to the nearest exit

🔆 Wake Lock: during emergency mode, the screen no longer turns off (browser Wake Lock API). You can also enable it permanently from ⚙️ Configuration → "Keep screen on".
tutorial.card13.hint: Emergency modes NEVER replace a call to rescue services. It's a backup tool to communicate your position to rescuers.
tutorial.card14.texte:
⚠️ 3 distinct "emergency" modes in MyKTAMap, don't confuse them:

  • ⛑️ I'm lost = YOU are looking for yourself
  • 🚨 Panic mode = YOU are panicking (see previous card)
  • 🚨 Rescue Mode = SOMEONE ELSE is lost, you coordinate the search

Access: sidebar → 🧭 Tracker (full-screen modal) → Emergency section → red 🚨 Rescue Mode button.

The scenario has 2 distinct states:

📝 State 1 — CREATION (cold planning OR on the spot):

  • Create a named scenario ("Search for Marc 05/26")
  • Add teams (NATO palette Alpha/Bravo/Charlie...) with entry + intermediate + exit route + search area + auto-computed route (Pathfinder avoids overlaps between teams)
  • Auto pre-fill from ⛑️ Lost Mode (last known position + uncertainty area)
  • Multi-level M-LVL supported (auto 1 team per floor if needed)
  • Export 3 formats: printable A4 PDF with mini-map + cross-app geolocated KMZ (Google Earth / OsmAnd) + standalone .mkmsec.json for cross-device sharing

🚀 State 2 — FIELD EXECUTION (incident triggered, real-time Live view):

  • "🚀 Launch the rescue plan" button + role selection modal
  • 👤 Surface operator: command post, overview of multi-team cards + status + last obs + "🚨 Take over" button with automatic return
  • 🚨 Team member: in the field, clickable visual stepper + observations + 7 quick statuses (All clear / Suspect / Blocked / Clue / Help requested / Forced turnaround / Victim found = blinking red card on the PC side) + photos (max 5/step, dedicated local IDB)
  • 🚑 Free responder: reinforcement with no pre-assigned team, chronological free-form notes with timestamps
  • Global timer with fair pause · "📦 PLAN ENDED" banner after stopping

📤 Report along the steps at any time (button in each Live view): printable PDF / standalone .mkmsec.report.json / clipboard text. 3 scopes depending on your role (global operator / team member only / responder notes).
tutorial.card14.hint: Phase 3 single-device for now. To share observations between surface operator and field team members, use .mkmsec.report.json (email / USB key / AirDrop).
tutorial.card15.texte:
Universal shortcut: Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on Mac) — opens the search bar from anywhere in the app. Toggle click again to close.

🎯 Searches 4 categories simultaneously:

  • 📍 Points: by name, ID, tag, description
  • 🛣️ Paths: by label, type, level
  • ⬛ Zones: by label, type, level
  • 🏛️ Structures: by label, type, level

📑 Results grouped by category, scored by relevance. Live auto-completion on every key pressed.

🎛️ Cumulative filters (chips above the list):

  • By category (points / paths / zones / structures)
  • By layer (My annotations, shafts.json, etc.)
  • By tag (ventilation shaft, room, crawlway…)

✨ Click on a result:

  • Point → centers the map + opens the popup + yellow circle 3s
  • Path / Zone / Structure → centers + yellow flash 4s overlay
tutorial.card16.texte:
Mark your important points of interest as favorites to access them in 1 click.

📝 How to add a favorite:

  • Click on a marker → popup → ⭐ Favorite button (toggle)
  • The star fills ⭐ and the point appears in the ⭐ Favorites group

📂 Accessing favorites:

  • Left sidebar → ⭐ Favorites group (just after M-LVL if active). Dynamic list updated on every add/remove.
  • Click a favorite → centers the map on the point + orange flash 3s + popup open

📤 JSON Export / Import: from 📊 Session details, you can export your favorites list as JSON then import it on another device (phone → computer, or share with a friend). Lightweight format, independent of the plan.

💡 Typical use cases:

  • Quarry main entrance (= "base")
  • Meeting point with a group
  • Bivouac room, drinking-water point
  • Trap / recently collapsed passage (to avoid)

🔒 Storage: local storage["myktamap_favoris_v1"] indexed by planId. Full snapshots of points = resilience even if the point is moved or deleted.
tutorial.card17.texte:
Computes the shortest path between N waypoints following the existing path network (Dijkstra algorithm + crossing enrichment).

🎯 3 ways to add a waypoint:

  • 🔍 Autocomplete in the route modal (search points by name/tag)
  • 🏷️ Exact ID entry + Add button
  • 📍 Click on the map (cyan floating mode)
  • 🧭 My position: takes your current tracker position as the start point

🚫 Avoidance preferences (optional):

  • Points: "do NOT go through this shaft"
  • Tags: "avoid all hazard-type passages"
  • Avoidance radius: margin around avoided points (0-500 px, default 100)

⛔ Inaccessible zones are automatically bypassed (hard constraint). Point/tag avoidances are soft constraints — if no path exists without them, the pathfinder still computes a path and flags that it had to go through them.

⚙️ Speed modes (affect the estimated time): 🤕 Injured 2 km/h / 🐌 Slow 3 km/h / 🚶 Normal 5 km/h / 🏃 Fast 7 km/h. +15 min break per intermediate waypoint.

📊 Distance + estimated time label at the bottom-left of the map. Neon cyan path with SVG drop-shadow halo.
tutorial.card18.texte:
3 complementary measurement tools:

📐 Distance measurement (right sidebar → 📐 Measure → 📐 Distance)

  • Click-click to place vertices, dashed magenta polyline
  • Live label 123.4 m or 1.23 km beyond 1 km
  • Angles between segments displayed
  • Persisted in session (available again on reload)

⬛ Area measurement (right sidebar → 📐 Measure → ⬛ Area)

  • Click to place polygon vertices. Shoelace algorithm.
  • Live label 1234 m² or 1.23 ha beyond 1 hectare
  • 2 EXCLUSIVE modes (distance OR area) — switching resets the points

📏 Total path distance (right sidebar → 🛣️ Paths → 📏)

  • Highlights in cumulative magenta all paths of a given type
  • Computes the total distance per type + grand total
  • Filterable: ☑ Main / ☑ Secondary / ☑ Trail
  • Includes ALL paths (session + embedded data layers, visible or hidden)

The px/m scale is set in the plan's tracking config (or default 1 px = 1 m).
tutorial.card19.texte:
If you map a quarry with several stacked floors, the multi-level mode is essential. Enabled at plan creation time (generator → "🏗️ Multi-level plan" checkbox) or manual plan-config.json edit.

📍 "Active level" button (left sidebar) — yellow badge with the number:

  • Click → management modal (active level single-select + visible levels multi-select)
  • Active level = where new annotations are drawn
  • Visible levels = what you see displayed (Quick actions "All" / "Active only")
  • Negative levels supported (basements -1, -2…). Extensible via − and + buttons

🪜 Inter-level junctions (right sidebar → 🛣️ Paths → 🪜):

  • Special path connecting 2 points on different levels (stairs, slope, internal shaft)
  • Always visible regardless of the level filter (= otherwise impossible to navigate between floors)
  • Magenta dashed style with round markers at the ends
  • The pathfinder uses them naturally to move from one level to another

📤 Exports respect the level filter: you can draw on 5 floors and export only the 2 in the middle. Per-level breakdown in 📊 Global stats.
tutorial.card19.hint: If your quarry is single-level, ignore this feature — left for advanced use only.
tutorial.card20.texte:
📊 Plan global stats (accessible from 📊 Session details → 📊 View global statistics):

  • Totals per category (points / paths / zones / structures)
  • Breakdown by tag (how many ventilation shafts, how many rooms, etc.)
  • Cumulative total distance + total area
  • If multi-level: per-level breakdown
  • 4 native inline SVG pie charts: point tags / path types / zone types / structure types distribution
  • 📤 A4 PDF tech-sheet export + 📊 CSV ZIP export (4 UTF-8 files + README, Excel-FR compatible ; separator)

🔥 Heatmap (Tracker menu → 🔥) — visual foot-traffic density:

  • 6 checkable sources: tracker timeline / session points / session paths / session zones / session structures / 4 data-layer sub-sources (points / paths / zones / structures, visible or not)
  • Radius sliders (10-120 px) + Intensity (0.2-3×)
  • Interpolation along segments (real continuous trails, not isolated blobs)
  • Auto normalization: densest pixel = red, least dense = blue (adapts to your data)
  • Tracker timeline filter: skip recalibrations (teleports), pauses >5min

💡 Multi-session accumulation: the tracker timeline is persisted between restarts → your heatmap builds up as you explore.
tutorial.card21.texte:
💾 Export modal (left sidebar → ⬆️ Save → 💾 Export) with 5 tabs: 🚀 Full · 🎨 Advanced · 🔄 Conversion · 🔗 Merge · 📡 External export.

📄 Full and Advanced tabs — re-importable into MyKTAMap:

  • Full mode: everything in one file (points + paths + zones + structures + measurements + tracker timeline + optional POI photos)
  • Advanced mode: granularity by layer, by tag, by type, choice to include or not the photos / tracker / measurements
  • Output: .json or .zip (if photos checked)

🌍 📡 External export → KMZ — for Google Earth, OsmAnd, Avenza, ArcGIS Earth, Locus:

  • Requires plan GPS calibration (2 plan↔GPS points, set in the generator)
  • Embeds the plan image + all Placemarks (points/lines/polygons) + per-tag icon style
  • The plan-level custom legend travels with the KMZ via an extra file myktamap-extras.json (ignored by third-party apps, restored on MyKTAMap re-import)

📤 📡 External export → GPX — for TopoDroid, OsmAnd, Strava, Garmin:

  • Universal GPX 1.1 format, full MyKTAMap roundtrip (tags via <sym>, M-LVL levels via <cmt>, descriptions, custom legend via <extensions>)
  • Reuses the KMZ calibration — if you configured KMZ, GPX works too

🔄 Conversion tab — converts your session to/from a data layer (devmap-data) ready to integrate into another plan-config.json. Tracker intentionally excluded (= frozen, read-only data layer).
tutorial.card22.texte:
🖼️ Image export modal (left sidebar → 🖼️) with 2 modes:

⚡ Quick mode:

  • Captures exactly what you see on the map (current layer visibility)
  • 1 click → downloaded PNG file
  • Ideal to quickly share a view

🎨 Advanced mode:

  • Granular filters: by image layer, by data layer, by point tag, by path/zone/structure type, by M-LVL level
  • Include the legend or not (3 styles: opaque / semi / watermark — the “print” style belongs to the PDF)
  • Format: PNG or JPG, custom resolution, 4 legend positions (4 corners)

📄 Printable PDF export:

  • 5 formats × 2 orientations: A0/A1/A2/A3/A4 portrait OR landscape
  • Plan + annotations + 4-corner legend overlay + optional header (title + metas)
  • Layer filters identical to advanced PNG
  • Dedicated "print" style (white background, max contrast, readable when printed)

💡 Typical use cases: A2/A3 print for the field (waterproof paper), PNG for Discord/email, PDF for long-term archiving or formal sharing.
tutorial.card23.texte:
The app has 3 levels of protection against data loss:

💾 Per-plan auto-save (local storage slot myktamap_session_v1_<planId>):

  • Silent save every 1.5 s (adaptive throttle if CPU busy)
  • 1 slot per plan = each plan keeps ITS session independently
  • On next launch, your session is auto-restored without intervention

📦 10 backups per plan, in your browser’s storage (oldest first):

  • Automatic snapshot every 5 min AND before a destructive action (clear session, reset, etc.)
  • Visible in 📊 Session details → 📦 Recent backups
  • Click ↻ Restore on a snapshot = reverts to that state (the app reloads the right plan + state automatically)
  • Manual: 📆 Snapshot now button to freeze an important state

⏪ Undo / Redo Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y:

  • 50 actions historized in RAM
  • Covers: add/edit/delete of points, paths, zones, structures
  • Also accessible via the ⏪ ⏩ buttons in the ⏪ History group of the left sidebar
  • Reset on plan switch (clean history per plan)

💡 If something goes wrong: 📊 Session details → 📦 Recent backups → ↻ Restore. Backups belong to each map and are deleted with it — export your session first.
tutorial.card24.titre: OSM View — your plan projected on OpenStreetMap
tutorial.card24.texte:
If your plan is GPS georeferenced (2-point lat/lng calibration), you can project it onto OpenStreetMap to see where it is in the real world — useful to locate a site entrance, spot the surface roads, brief a rescue team unfamiliar with the cavity.

🌍 2 usage contexts:

  • Fullscreen modal (from map mode): 🌍 button in the top bar → OSM View modal with your plan as a transparent overlay (opacity slider), your POIs, your paths, your zones and structures. Plan V2 tiles + category filters + multi-level M-LVL.
  • HOME widget: mini-map embedded in your home page with a plan selector + ⛶ fullscreen button. You see your georeferenced plans at a glance without loading.

📍 "My GPS position" button in both contexts: on-demand single fix (no continuous watch = 0 battery impact), cyan-blue marker + accuracy circle. Safeguard: refuses if you are kilometers from the plan (e.g. Paris Catacombs plan while you're in Lyon).

🏷️ Tag filter: chips in the banner (POI by category). Consistent with the map mode filter but independent (OSM filter local to the modal or widget).

🛡️ The only screen that goes online: OSM View requests the background tiles from tile.openstreetmap.org — nothing else, none of your data. It is on by default since v1.90.2; you can turn it off in ⚙️ Configuration → 🗺️ OSM View (OpenStreetMap). Strict offline and incognito modes block it automatically.
tutorial.card24.hint: © OpenStreetMap contributors attribution shown in the corner of the maps — ODbL obligation respected. Without plan GPS calibration, OSM View is not available (nothing to project).
tutorial.card25.titre: History Mode — Free note + plan PDF
tutorial.card25.texte:
History Mode lets you tell the story of your plan: historical context, anecdotes, sources, testimonies, site-specific instructions.

📖 2 complementary formats:

  • Free note (inline Markdown editor): headings, lists, links, bold / italic, code blocks. Auto-save, persisted locally per plan.
  • PDF documents (up to 10 per plan): import your PDFs (original survey, historical IGN map, trip report, geological study…). They stack up — a new import no longer overwrites the previous one — and a list lets you switch between them. your browser’s local storage storage, embedded display (sandboxed iframe). The PDF shipped in the ZIP by the plan author sits on top (📕, not deletable) and no longer prevents you from adding your own.

📖 Access: 📖 button in the sidebar (next to the stats), same size as the other header chips. Visible when the plan has a note OR an associated PDF. Otherwise, the button directly opens the edit modal to get started.

💾 Included in your exports: the free note and the History PDF are embedded in MKMSESSION exports (Full session ZIP) — so you can transmit all the context with your session.

🔇 100% local: the PDF stays in your browser’s local storage on your device, never transmitted anywhere. If you switch devices, import it from your MKMSESSION.
tutorial.card25.hint: Ideal for plans inherited from a former colleague: you can tell the story of the site and attach the original survey in a single exportable "bag".
tutorial.card26.titre: My logbook — the history of your trips
tutorial.card26.texte:
Auto-save keeps the current state of a plan. The logbook keeps the history: every time you explore a plan, a trip is archived. Clearing a session does not delete trips already filed.

📔 A trip contains: the date, the time actually spent in the app, the distance travelled with the tracker, the points / paths / zones added, the photos taken, the path you walked, and a free-form note you can write even weeks later.

🚶 Field trip or 🖥️ desk work? The logbook tells them apart on its own: if the tracker recorded movement it is a field trip; if you only annotated without moving (prep at home) it is desk work, filed separately. Totals count field trips only. Got it wrong (a trip made with the tracker off)? A button on the trip sheet fixes the classification.

📔 Where: the 📔 My logbook tile on the home screen, in the « 🧰 Tools » card (visible on mobile too). From a plan: Session modal → 📔 Trip in progress, with 🏁 Close my trip to file it right away.

📖 2nd tab: Stories — your free notes and plan PDFs (History Mode) gathered across all plans, readable and editable without loading the plan.

🔇 100% local: nothing is uploaded. A very short trip that left no trace is not kept, and the logbook starts empty — it cannot reconstruct your trips from before it existed.
tutorial.card26.hint: The logbook answers "what did I do on July 12th?" — a question the app simply could not answer before.
tutorial.card27.texte:
To go further, the app has many additional tools:

⚙️ ⚙️ Loader Configuration (button on the home page):

  • 🖼️ Tiling Mode: performance preset (auto / quality / balanced / performance / off)
  • 🚀 ULTRA Mode: 6 fine-grain toggles for large plans (decimation, skip animations, viewport culling, etc.)
  • 📊 Memory inspector: full transparency on what is stored locally (local storage, your browser’s local storage, PWA Cache). 📋 Copy report button.
  • 🔒 Network audit: LIVE log of every request sent + "strict offline" mode that blocks anything non-whitelisted
  • 🎨 Light theme: dark/light toggle, persisted locally
  • 🔆 Wake Lock: keeps the screen on (useful in a cavity)
  • 🔄 Soft force update: purges the PWA cache without touching your data
  • 💥 Reset everything: full wipe (local storage + IDB + caches). Double confirmation required.

⚙️ ⚙️ Map mode settings (left sidebar): per-plan preferences (debug, performance, M-LVL if applicable, etc.).

🔐 Optional local access code: 4-6 digit PIN + Face ID / Touch ID / Windows Hello (WebAuthn). Protection at app startup, ideal if you lend your phone.

🎤 Voice command: floating mic button at the bottom-right of map mode. Say "go to [POI]", "enable tracker", "emergency exit" and the app executes. Uses the browser's native Web Speech API, no audio leaves your device. Auto-stop after the command runs to save battery. iOS Safari supported (with proper mic release on stop).

🪫 Haptic vibration: toggle in Configuration. Vibrates on 5 critical events (arrival at destination, emergency mode, etc.). Discreet, non-intrusive.

📋 Crash reports: if the app was killed by the OS (mobile OOM typically), the report is archived in 📊 Memory inspector → Latest crashes section. Copyable to send to the author via the contact page.

🔎 Home search bar: centered in the header, it searches a point across all your plans without opening any — results show up live under the bar, Enter or 🔎 for the full search.
