aide.sec.histoire.html:
📖 button to the left of the battery 🔋 → 2-tab modal, specific to each map:

  • 📝 Free note — auto-saved Markdown notebook (headings, bold, lists, links, quotes). Preview mode to read / ✏️ Edit to modify the source.
  • 📚 History — up to 10 PDF documents per map (before, only one, and a new import overwrote the previous). List above the viewer, 📥 Import adds, 🗑️ Remove deletes the displayed document. The PDF shipped in the ZIP sits on top (📕, not deletable) and no longer blocks adding your own. Warning past 25 MB total, refusal past 100 MB. On iPhone: ↗️ Open in a tab button for native full screen.

Free note + PDF are automatically included in the session export (.mkmsession.zip) → everything travels with your session for sharing or transfer. 100% offline.
aide.sec.sortie-urgence.titre: 🚨 Emergency Exit Mode — The nearest exit
aide.sec.sortie-urgence.html:
🚨 button between 📖 History Mode and the battery 🔋. Tap it (or say "exit" by voice 🎤) and the app:

  1. Scans POIs tagged as open exits (cao, peo, eso) or entrée.
  2. Computes the actual navigable path via the pathfinder (handles walls and inter-level junctions).
  3. Displays the nearest one + 🧭 Plot the route button + collapsible See the N other exits.

Starting point = your position at that very moment, without asking, as soon as tracking is active or you have located yourself once since opening the map (📍 I am here, recalibration, portal). Never confirmed (= still the map's start point) → only then does the app ask “Where are you?”: one tap on the map, which also recalibrates tracking. The modal says where the computation starts from. Multi-level OK. Confirmation vibration. Closed versions (caf/pef/esf) ignored. 100% offline.
aide.sec.aide-doc-legende.html:
❓This help — button reference 📖User documentation 🤖AI Help — download a context file to paste into ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini/etc. 🗺️Legend of the map's icons 🚨Public alert (loader button, left of 📖) — shows the current alert, or "No alert in progress" if the situation is OK 🔒Lock the application (loader button, right of ⚙️) — if a local access code is set, stops active modules and restarts MyKTAMap: the PIN prompt shows at startup and the code must be re-entered to resume. If no code is set, a modal invites you to create one from ⚙️ Configuration. 🏷️Version badge (loader footer) — click to view the update modal or the notes of the installed version. Blinks blue if a new version is available.

🚨 Public alerts: if the author broadcasts an alert (fire, closure, toxic gas...), a pulsing red modal appears automatically after the splash, with title, message and instructions. 3 possible levels: emergency (red pulse, critical situation), warning (orange) or info (blue). The 🚨 button in the loader header lets you re-read the alert at any time, OR check "✅ No alert in progress" if the situation has returned to normal. Once "Got it" is clicked, the modal no longer reappears on reload as long as the alert is the same — unless the author publishes a new one.

🛡️ Revoked maps (anti-leak): if a ZIP map leaks massively (public Telegram, forum, etc.), the author can revoke it server-side. When the ZIP is imported, the app computes its SHA-256 fingerprint locally and compares it against the public denylist.json list downloaded at boot. On a match → blocking red modal with reason + date + a "Got it, delete this map" button that automatically removes the map from your list. Also covers the generator ("Edit an existing map"). 🔄 Auto audit at startup: already-imported maps are also checked ~2s after boot. If one of them has been revoked since your last import, it is deleted automatically and an orange modal informs you (reason + date). Strict privacy: 0 fingerprints sent to the server. List viewable at https://myktamap.fr/denylist.json.

🔎 Search. The 📖 Documentation modal has a full-text search field: every occurrence is highlighted, Enter or ↓ jumps to the next one, and table-of-contents entries without a match fade out. Accents do not matter (“reglages” finds “Réglages”). Right here, the hub search looks in the titles and content of the sections.
aide.sec.parametres.html:
⚙️One screen, eight groups — 🌍 Application · 📐 Map: scale & geolocation · 📍 Navigation & tracker · 🎨 Display · 🚀 Performance · 🛰️ Sensor options · 🔒 Privacy & security · 🛠️ System. Every title carries its scope (📍 this map / 🌍 all maps) and collapses with a tap (remembered). Everything is saved as you change it: no Apply button anymore; an out-of-range value turns red and is not written. Esc, ✕ or Close to leave. 🏠Set from the home screen — language, theme, zoom-scaled icons, anchored panels, snapping, outings logbook: their value is shown here, read-only, with a button to go change them in ⚙️ Configuration (leaves the map, the session is kept). 📐Map — Scale (px/m) with 🎯 calibration, 🧭 map North (field or 2-click picker), and 🌐 GPS georeferencing in its own sub-modal (state shown: georeferenced A/B/C or not). The calibration entered here pre-fills 📡 External export. 📍Navigation & tracker — start point (🔍 via a point, 📍 map click: tracking restarts from there), step detection (length, threshold, delay — bounded), smart navigation and its tolerances. All per map. 🎬Presentation mode — button at the very top; F key on PC. Exit: F / Esc or floating ✕ button. 🔆Keep the screen on and 🎤 Voice commands (all maps) — when the browser does not support them (Firefox), the line stays visible, greyed out, with the reason — like 🔋 battery and 📳 vibration. 🚀ULTRA performance (per map) — 🚀 ULTRA applies 7 optimizations at once, or one by one; on a multi-level map, “🏗️ Show every level at launch” (applied at the next load).

↺ Default values only touches this map (scale, pedometer, start, smart navigation, North) and puts tracking back at the start — confirmation asked. Home-screen settings do not move. The full reset and the 🔐 Local access code stay in the home ⚙️ Configuration.
aide.sec.recherche.html:
📍Points (name, id, tag, description, state) 🛣️Paths (label, type, M-LVL level) ⬛Zones (type, level) 🏛️Structures (pillars, walls, faces) 🌐GPS coordinates — paste 48.6808, 2.1588 directly (Google Maps format). If the map is georeferenced: a POI within 50 px → "Go to point"; otherwise → "Create a point here" → opens the form pre-filled at that position

Search covers 4 categories + GPS. Ctrl+K keyboard shortcut (Cmd+K on Mac) to open/close instantly. Results grouped by category with counters. On click: centers + visual flash (circle for points, dashed polyline for paths, transparent polygon for zones / pillars). Filter by category + layer + tag.

🌐 GPS format: this same lat, lng format is accepted in ⚙️ Settings → Georeferencing, in the 📡 External export modal (KMZ/GPX) and when creating a georeferenced map — paste from Google Maps, the app splits the 2 values automatically.
aide.sec.charger-import.html:
📥Import — a single button that opens a 2-card modal: 📥 MyKTAMap session (.json / .zip with photos) or 📤 External GPX (TopoDroid, OsmAnd, Avenza, Strava, Garmin… requires GPS calibration). Preview before import, Ctrl+Z to undo. 📊Map data editor — edit the data (points, paths, zones) as a table. Also holds 🔗 Merge data layers (moved in from the home screen). 🧭Switch map — no longer here: tap the compass rose or the map title in the top bar (session saved automatically)

Multi-map: every map you load (server or local ZIP) is remembered in your personal list. When you return to the home, you find:

  • ▶️ Resume — relaunches the last opened map in one click.
  • 🔎 Search bar — centered in the header: search a point across ALL your maps — live results under the bar from 2 characters, Enter or 🔎 for the full search.
  • 📔 My logbook — tile in the 🧰 Tools card: the history of your trips plus your map notes and PDFs.
  • 📅 Recent — the last 5 maps used.
  • 📂 All — all your known maps.
  • 🌐 = server map · 💾 = local ZIP map.
  • 💾 Export / 📂 Import your list to share or migrate it.

Server maps — the app automatically detects maps published on the server and offers them in your list.

Local maps — when you click a local map, two cases depending on the box ticked at the initial load:

  • ✅ Saved — the ZIP is copied into the browser (setting ⚙️ Home configuration → "💾 Store the map in the app on first load", on by default). Reloads in 0 clicks, works even offline and on mobile. Storage limit depends on the browser (~50 MB iOS, several GB Android/desktop).
  • 📁 Re-selection — the ZIP is requested on every click (drag & drop or click the area). When the setting is off.

📱 iPhone — for maximum persistence, install the app as a PWA (Share → Add to Home Screen) before saving the map.

🔄 Re-importing a regenerated map — a ZIP with the same name + same author as a map already in your list, but a different version, opens a choice: 🔄 Update (replaces the entry and its stored archive — session, notes and links kept), ➕ Keep both, or Cancel (default on ✕ / Escape / click outside: no accidental overwrite). Same name AND version = direct update without asking, as before.

💾 Retrieve a map's ZIP — the profile export does not carry archives. If you lost the original ZIP, open ℹ️ Info on the map: a 💾 Download the ZIP button gives it back, provided it was saved in the app. On a map using "permanent access" or re-selection the button is greyed out — the app holds nothing, the file lives (or lived) on your disk.

📦 Import several maps — button in the 🧰 Tools section of the home screen. Pick N ZIP archives: they enter your list one by one, without any of them opening. The screen first shows what will be added, what is already there and what is refused, with the size and the space left; it refuses to start if it does not fit, and stops right there, keeping the maps already added, if space runs out. Duplicates are settled once for the whole batch: leave as is, replace, or keep both. The 💾 Preload the ZIP box (checked by default) keeps the file: the map then opens from the list without picking its ZIP again; unchecked, nothing is stored and the ZIP is asked for on first opening.
aide.sec.import-sig.html:
🗺️Drop a .geojson or .kml on the "📦 Load a new map" area of the home screen (the same one you use for ZIPs) → the conversion panel opens. Also works from the Generator import area 🖼️No image needed: a blank background is generated and aligned on the file's coordinates 🏷️Mapping screen: pick the column holding the type, then say what each value means

⚠️ GPS coordinates required (WGS84 / EPSG:4326). In QGIS: Export → Save Features As… then EPSG:4326 in the CRS field. A file in Lambert 93 is converted automatically; any other projection is refused, with the number of offending coordinates — accepting it would place your map thousands of kilometres away with no warning.

Offered values are split by family (the most likely types come first). ⚠️ Routing is FREE: a polygon can also become a path, and a line a quarry face — the shape in the file does not say what the object IS. Polygon holes ignored, 20,000-object cap. Shapefile and GeoPackage unsupported: they would require heavy libraries, incompatible with 100% offline. Re-export as GeoJSON.

🔄 Fixing an imported layer. The survey shipped in a ZIP is read-only. Under 🔍 Filters → Data layers, “🔄 Edit” copies the layer into your session: you fix it on screen (a quarry face that is really a gallery, say), then “💾 Export” hands you a file to give back to the plan in the Generator, on that layer’s row. The original hides itself to avoid duplicates, “↩️ Restore” undoes everything, and the app tells you the weight before acting.

🗺️ Quarry surveys. Lambert 93 (EPSG:2154, metre coordinates) is converted automatically — other projections are still rejected. Pick a level column so each floor keeps its own: a preview shows the breakdown before generating, and “one colour per level” stops six stacked floors from blending (renameable on the spot with 🏷️ — and your names, your colours and the types you add yourself are kept in the generated plan; if the screen says the legend has been reset, a change in the mapping has invalidated your names, reopen 🏷️ before generating). An object's shape does not say what it is: a polygon may become a zone, a pillar, a wall or a working face — each value targets the family you choose. The plan height is computed from the width, so content stays inside the frame. ⚠️ A plan created from a GPX or SIG file with an older version of the app carries a wrong scale: regenerate it for correct distances.
aide.sec.creer-modifier-plan.html:
🏗️Open the map generator (direct click)

The generator now guides you step by step (Next / Previous / Skip) with a final summary flagging what is missing before generating; an imported ZIP pre-fills every step, and 🗒️ Show all restores the classic one-page layout (choice remembered). Lets you create a new map or edit an existing one from a ZIP archive. 2 modes — 🚀 Simple (just image + name + version + V2/M-LVL → ZIP ready in 30 sec) and ⚙️ Advanced (layers, tracking, icons, GPS georef, 🏷️ map legend). Choice remembered locally. Edit mode always forces Advanced to preserve the source map's customizations.

🗺️ A GeoTIFF can be dropped as is. Pick a .tif / .tiff georeferenced in QGIS as the map image: the app reads the georeferencing written in the file and sets the GPS calibration, the scale (px/m) and the extent without asking — no more entering the GPS points twice. Read: LZW, Deflate or no compression, 8 bits per channel, greyscale / RGB / RGBA, strip-organised image, north-up rotation-free georeferencing, coordinates in Lambert 93, Web Mercator or WGS84. Anything else is refused in plain words, with what to re-export. 100 % local: the file is read and converted in your browser.
aide.sec.bibliotheque-plans.html: ⭐Pin — the star on each row moves the map to the top of the list; click again to unpin 🏷️Tags — free labels per map (ℹ️ Info → "Map tags", comma-separated). As soon as one map is tagged, filter chips appear above the list. Stored in the app, they travel with the profile export; a ZIP generated with the Generator's 🏷️ Tags field proposes them on import, never overwriting the ones you set. They are also used in the OSM view: one click on a label shows every plan carrying it, a second click removes them 📁Folders — All | Folders switch right of the title. In Folders mode, arrange your maps in sections of your own (➕), with a colour; a map lives in one folder, the others in "Unfiled". To file: drag the row onto a folder (mouse on PC, long press by touch), or ☑ Select one or more maps then "Move to…". ⋮ on a header: rename, colour, order, delete (no map is ever deleted), and a tag rule that files tagged maps on its own. The dot before the name tells you: filled = filed by hand (or by the multi-import, or the server), hollow = brought in by a rule — it follows its tags, remove the tag and it leaves the folder. Folders travel with the profile; those proposed by a server cannot be renamed or deleted while it declares them, but you always move your maps. 🔎Filter by name — field above the list, filters live as you type ✏️Rename display — in ℹ️ Info: a local name to tell two identically-named maps apart (two "Catacombs" from different authors). The map's real name is left untouched; empty field = back to the original 📚Importing a same-name map — the "This map already exists" popup always fires: Update / Keep both / cancel. No more silent overwrite 🗑️Remove a map — at the bottom of the ℹ️ Info window with confirmation (the row ✕ is gone — no more accidental removal). The ZIP on your disk is untouched
aide.sec.profil.html:
👤Profile banner in the loader header (above "My maps") — avatar + nickname + global mini-stats (📍 points · 🛣️ paths · ⬛ zones · 🏛️ structures + cumulative time, kept) 🏅Rank / badge (Tourist → Grandmaster) based on your time spent, maps explored and km of gallery — colored ring + medal on the photo, and the breakdown (3 metrics + progress + score) in the profile card 🏆Achievements — 32 to unlock: 8 families × 4 tiers (🥉🥈🥇👑, maps/km/time/POIs/paths/zones/structures) + 6 « 🎉 Special » one-shot (Jack of all trades, Centurion, Mole, Multi-level, Marathon, Completionist). Toast on unlock + N/38 grid in the profile card. Score + achievement count can be shown in the banner stats (🎨 Banner stats) ✏️Click the nickname or the avatar → editing modal (free nickname + profile photo upload) 🖼️Profile photo auto-compressed (max 512px, JPEG q88) — otherwise the default avatar = the nickname's initial in a colored circle 📦Profile exportable / importable — share between devices without a server

100% local storage in a dedicated local store — nickname + photo + dates. No data transmitted. Default profile empty (👤 anonymous): no existing user is forced to configure anything. Banner stats: from 2 stats available the banner displays them in mobile median, cumulative time survives reloads.

🖼️ Home wallpaper — at the bottom of the Profile modal you can set your own image instead of the theme colour. Three settings: the veil (darkens the image to keep text readable — 0% = bare image, 100% = the previous plain background), and framing ↔ / ↕. That last one matters: the screen never shows the whole photo (it is scaled up to cover, the rest is cropped) — in portrait, a landscape photo only shows about a quarter of its width. Only the slider for the overflowing axis has an effect. The image stays on the device, in the same storage as the avatar, and re-encoding strips its metadata (including where it was taken). ⚠️ It does not travel with the profile export yet.
aide.sec.favoris.html:
⭐Button in a POI's popup — toggle ☆ inactive / ⭐ active (amber) ⭐Left sidebar group (right after M-LVL) — side flyout listing the current map's favorites 🎯Click a favorite → centers the map + flashes an orange circleMarker for 3 s + opens the original marker's popup

Remembered locally per map. Full copy of the points (id, name, coordinates, tag, layer) — resilient if the point is moved or removed from the map. Not shared via exports (= a local view per device). Persistent across sessions and survives a reload.
aide.sec.historique-undo.html:
⏪Undo the last action (Ctrl+Z) — up to 50 actions ⏩Redo the undone action (Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z)

Covers the 4 categories of drawable annotations — ✏️ points, 🛣️ paths, ⬛ zones, 🏛️ structures. Atomic granularity (1 click = 1 undoable). A discreet toast on every action. Sidebar buttons auto-greyed when the stack is empty. History not saved: starts from scratch on reload, auto-reset when switching map. ⚠️ Photos excluded (irreversible deletion).
aide.sec.batterie.html:
⚡Header chip — charging (green) 🪫Header chip — discharging (color according to level) 🔋🔋 STATUS block of emergency mode (level + state shown large)

3 display points: new interface header (⚡/🪫 chip next to session counters), 📋 Active session modal footer, 🔋 STATUS block of emergency mode. Graduated warnings via toast at 20% / 10% / 5% (once per threshold per discharge cycle). ⚠️ Limited compatibility: the browser's battery feature is available in Chromium only (Android Chrome, PC Chrome/Edge). On Safari iOS and recent Firefox, it was removed for privacy reasons — the chip is then hidden, with no error message.
aide.sec.stats-session.html:
📊Stats block at the top of the 📋 Active session modal 📋Copy the summary to the clipboard (plain text, ready for Discord / SMS / email) 💾TXT export — downloads a .txt file with the full summary

Display: total annotations, breakdown by type (📍 points · 🛣️ paths · ⬛ zones · 🏛️ structures), cumulative distance of paths (auto m → km), cumulative area of zones (auto m² → ha), attached POI photos, time elapsed since the session started. In multi-level (M-LVL), an additional per-level breakdown is shown.

📊 Session details (tap the counters in the top bar) has become the map's dashboard: at the top, ✅ Saved N s ago (red if saving fails); aggregated stats and per-level breakdown; your points, paths by type with distance, zones, structures and photos; other measurements; 📔 Current outing (🏁 Close, 🧭 Refine, open the logbook); ⭐ Favorites (export this map / all, import); 📦 Recent backups of this map (↻ Restore, 📆 Snapshot now, 🗑️ Clear all — every deletion asks for confirmation); and the 📊 Global stats button (report, CSV, PDF).
aide.sec.inspecteur-memoire.html:
📊"📊 View memory state" button in ⚙️ loader Configuration (home) → new 📊 Inspector section 🗂️localStorage: MyKTAMap keys sorted by size + mini proportion bar 💾IndexedDB: 3 databases (handles / backups / photos) + native scan of third-party databases, count per store 📦PWA cache: list of caches, active cache marked (★), sample of the first 12 assets 📈Storage estimate: browser usage / quota with a color bar (green → yellow → red) 🧠Runtime: loaded map, active session (📍/🛣️/⬛/🏛️), loaded/missing JS modules 📋📋 Copy report button → plain markdown-like text ready to paste into Discord / email / GitHub

A transparency + debug tool. Shows a readable overview of everything MyKTAMap has written locally in your browser. Handy for diagnosing a bug ("my session disappears", "my photos are gone") or checking that a full reset really purged everything. Read-only, 100% local — no data transmitted.
aide.sec.legende.html:
✏️3-level cascade: session > map > MKM default (each level overrides the next) 📐Session editing (personal, local): 🖼️ PNG Export modal → "Customize labels" or the ✏️ Edit button in the 🗺️ map-mode Legend 🏗️Map-level editing (shared with all users of the map): map Generator in Advanced mode → "🏷️ Map legend" section ✨4 categories covered: 📍 icons / 🛣️ paths / ⬛ zones / 🏛️ structures — rename, hide, or add custom drawable entries 🌍KMZ round-trip: the map legend travels with your exported KMZ → auto-restored when re-imported into another MyKTAMap instance. Ignored by Google Earth / OsmAnd / Avenza. 📤GPX round-trip: same for GPX via the GPX file's metadata. Compatible with TopoDroid, OsmAnd, Strava, etc. 👁️On re-import (KMZ or GPX), the summary/preview explicitly shows "✅ Map custom legend detected: N renamed · M hidden · K customs" before generating the MyKTAMap ZIP.

Use case: a cataphile creating a quarry map can rename "Water" to "Bottom lake", hide the types they never use, and add their own drawable types ("Votive niche", "Stela", etc.). These customizations apply automatically to everyone who loads their map, in KMZ as well as GPX. Each user can still override their own session on top without breaking anything.
aide.sec.menu-tracker.html: 🧭The 🧭 Tracker button opens a full-screen modal of large tiles (instead of the old side menu) — clearer and more touch-friendly on mobile. 📋3 sections: Tracking (start/stop, recalibrate, My position, path lock) · Tools (compass, route, replay, heatmap) · Emergency (red). 📊Header: tracking state (on/off) + distance travelled + step count. ✕Close: cross, click outside, or Esc key. Tapping a tile closes the menu then runs the action. 🗺️Oriented map (Tools tile): while tracking, the map turns so your walking direction points to the top of the screen. Off by default; the map goes back upright as soon as tracking stops or you pick a tap tool. 🎯 Recenter button if you move the map.
aide.sec.replay-tracker.html:
🎬Replay button in the 🧭 Tracker group — opens the full-screen modal ▶️Play / Pause / Restart / End — timeline slider + speed selector 0.5× → 10× ⛶Toggle compact mode (bottom sheet) ↔ normal mode — to free up the map during replay 💾CSV export — file with timestamp + coordinates + type (+ level in M-LVL)

During tracking, the app records an internal timeline of events: start, each PDR step applied, each recalibration. On clicking 🎬, you replay your session with a moving yellow marker. Multi-segment trail: recalibrations (teleports) are visually skipped — no artificial straight line. Keyboard shortcuts: Space = play/pause · ← → = seek 1s · Esc = close. Not saved: starts from scratch on reload, reset when switching map.
aide.sec.enregistrer.html:
💾Export — modal with 5 tabs: 🚀 Full · 🎨 Advanced · 🔄 Conversion · 🔗 Merge (merges N data layer files into 1 file per type — also accessible from the home screen) · 📡 External export (KMZ + GPX). The Full export embeds the complete tracker timeline (route + dated temporal timeline + departure time) → lets you carry the GPS history between devices (multi-session heatmap + multi-device replay). Ignored in layer conversion. 📡Tracker checkbox — Advanced mode — in the 🖼️ Image export modal, the "Tracker position" checkbox shows the path's point counter (e.g. "+ path 142 pts") to visualize what will be burned onto the image. 🖼️Export to PNG/JPG — modal with Quick / Advanced mode 📤Export to printable PDF — A0 to A4 × portrait/landscape, legend positionable in a corner

📤 PDF: 10 formats (A0/A1/A2/A3/A4 × portrait/landscape), choice of data layers + image case by case, 4-corner overlay legend with 3 sizes and 4 styles (including 🆕 "Pro white background" by default for paper printing). Reuses the same rendering chain as the advanced PNG export for perfect visual consistency.

🌍 Your survey sits at its real depth. In a KMZ, altitude was written as zero: the survey floated over the vineyards in Google Earth. It now sits below the surface, at its level’s depth. 🧭 In GPX, deliberately no altitude: the format counts it above sea level, so writing “-30” for a gallery under a 100 m hill would announce a point 130 m too low — plausible to the eye, therefore undetectable. The depth goes into the description, read by a human.
aide.sec.tracker.html:
The Tracker group opens as a full-screen modal of tiles (see "🧭 Tracker menu") grouping its 11 actions. Order, top to bottom:

▶️⏹️Play / Stop — start / stop tracking via PDR sensors (experimental). Dynamic icon ▶️↔⏹️ depending on the state 🧭Compass — toggle of the magnetic North widget (useful orientation underground) 📍Recalibration mode — click the map or an existing point to reposition the marker. Auto-close after click + automatic return to compass 🎯My position — recenters the map on the tracker's current position (zoom kept). Works even when the tracker is stopped 🔓Suspend the path lock — temporarily disables locking onto paths (30 s / 1 min / 10 min / until re-enabled), with a countdown in the bottom bar 🗺️Compute a route — opens the route modal (waypoints, speed mode, avoidances) 🎬Tracker session replay — full-screen modal: timeline slider + play/pause + speed 0.5×→10× + CSV export. Compact mode auto on Play to free up the map. Shortcuts Space / ← → / Esc 🔥Density heatmap — interpolated segments + auto normalization + 6 checkable sources: 🚶 Tracker timeline · ✏️ Session points · 🛣️ Paths · ⬛ Zones · 🏛️ Structures · 📊 Data layers ⛑️I'm lost — RED BACKGROUND (emergency) — computes a probable zone of your position from your last known position, the time elapsed and visual clues 🚨XL "panic" emergency mode — RED BACKGROUND (emergency) — XL display of position + compass heading + auto-focus minimap + 🔋 battery + 🗺️ route toggle

🚨 Visual demarcation: the last 2 buttons (⛑️ and 🚨) are placed at the end of the menu with a distinctive red background to separate them from the normal navigation functions.

🚨 "Panic" emergency mode: a distinctive red button, different from ⛑️ "I'm lost" (which computes a zone). Here we assume you know where you are (the tracker shows it) but that you panic and need vital info in large print: XL position (map coords), large compass heading (direction of travel, needle turned), auto-focus minimap with the roads / zones / structures of the map in the background (useful to spot paths, exits, hazards). Automatic Wake Lock (the screen doesn't turn off). Sensor permissions auto-requested if not already granted. Exit via the ✕.

⛑️ Emergency mode: a distinctive orange sub-action. You indicate where you were (search for an existing point, click on the map or tracker position), how long ago, and the app draws an orange search circle around it (radius = speed × time, with no margin). The speed is chosen via 4 presets (selector) — same values as the route mode for consistency: 🤕 Injured (2 km/h), 🐌 Slow (3 km/h), 🚶 Normal (5 km/h, default), 🏃 Fast (7 km/h). Max time elapsed 1h30 (beyond that the zone becomes huge and irrelevant). You can add visual clues ("water can", "ram graffito"...) — the app searches for these words in the name, description and tags of the map's points; the clues that match inside the zone appear in pulsing purple, and their center gives a refined probable location. The 👁️ Close button closes the modal while keeping the zone visible on the map (to explore). The 🗑️ Clear the zone button (in the results) removes everything. Copyable text report to the clipboard (📋) for offline sharing (radio, SMS). A 📚 Best practices accordion at the top of the modal gathers the essential tips (stay calm, retrace your steps, look for the main axes/main galleries, use a physical compass, save your light, warn someone if you get a signal, what not to do). ⚠️ Geometric estimate only — it does NOT replace a real rescue operation (guide line, compass, spare lamp, paper map).

👣 The pedometer counted steps while standing still. On plans created from a GPX, KMZ or GIS file, the detection threshold was wrong: phone lying flat, it produced up to 10 km/h of imaginary distance. Plans already created are repaired when opened, nothing to regenerate. ⚠️ Distances already recorded in your logbook stay wrong: they cannot be recomputed afterwards.
aide.sec.mode-secours.html:
An operational coordination tool to organize search teams in case of an underground incident (lost cataphile, organized rescue). 3 distinct emergency modes not to be confused: ⛑️ I'm lost = YOU are looking for yourself · 🚨 Panic mode = YOU are panicking · 🚨 Rescue Mode = SOMEONE ELSE is lost and you organize the rescue.

📝 State 1 — CREATION (Edit view) — preparation/planning of the rescue plan.

🚨Opens the Rescue Mode modal (multi-scenarios per map, max 10 saved, oldest first) ➕Scenario creation: name + incident time + context notes 🎨Fixed 10-color NATO palette: Alpha red / Bravo blue / Charlie green / Delta yellow / Echo magenta / Foxtrot cyan / Golf orange / Hotel purple / India brown / Juliet grey 📍Teams with routes: entry + intermediates + exit (POI autocomplete / ID input / map click). Loop if entry=exit ⬛Search zone per team: polygon OR selected paths. A "POIs in zone" mini-modal auto-suggests intermediates 🗺️Route computed automatically with avoidances between teams (anti-overlap). Warning toast if avoidance is impossible 🏗️M-LVL level per team: ground/+1/-1 chip + editable select. Auto-creation of 1 team per level via the "🏗️ Auto" button 🔥Activity heatmap (tracker/POI/paths sources) to identify probable zones to search ⛑️Chaining I'm lost → Rescue: a button in I'm lost pre-fills the last known position + uncertainty zone + incident time ⭐Map favorites for quick access in the waypoint picker (max 8 chips above the search) 🔍Ctrl+K → assign a POI to a team in 2 clicks: 📌 button in the unified search results if Rescue Mode is active 🛑Configurable pause (shared with the main route): 0-120 min between intermediate stops, auto-recompute of durations

📤 3 export formats: 📄 Printable PDF A4 1 page/team with a thumbnail map + integrated mini-legend + empty observation box for paper field use · 🌍 Geolocated cross-app KMZ (Google Earth / OsmAnd / Avenza) with 43 NATO color styles + map as a 60% GroundOverlay + nested folders toggleable per team · 📦 standalone .mkmsec.json to share between devices without the whole session (preview modal BEFORE injection).

🚀 State 2 — FIELD EXECUTION (real-time Live view) — the incident is triggered, you follow the observations.

🚀Launch the rescue plan button in the Edit view → role selection modal 👤Surface Operator mode (PC lead): overview of multi-team cards + status + last obs + "🚨 Take over" button with automatic return 🚨Team member mode (in the field): clickable visual stepper + observations + 7 quick statuses + photos (max 5/step) + prev/next navigation 🚑Free rescuer mode (reinforcement without a team): loose chronological notes DESC + 7 quick buttons + auto timestamps ⏱️Global timer with a fair pause (excludes the cumulative pause time) 📤Report as steps progress: 3 formats (PDF/JSON/clipboard Text) × 3 levels (operator/team member/rescuer). Reusable at any time during or after the stop 📦PLAN COMPLETED banner in the Edit view after the stop: "📤 View historical report" + "🚀 Relaunch"

7+1 step statuses: • pending (default) · 🟢 All clear · 🟡 Suspicious · ⬛ Blocked · 🔵 Clue · 🟠 Help requested · 🟣 Forced turnaround · 🚨 Victim found (absolute emergency = flashing red card on the PC lead side).

📸 Photo storage dedicated to rescue mode: max 5 photos per step, auto JPEG q85 compression max 1920px, reused full-screen viewer.

📥 Consolidation between devices: back from the field, each team member exports their report via 📤 Report (team member level). The operator imports it in the Live Op view via the 📥 Import team member report button in the footer → preview modal with conflict detection → merge (observations concatenated and dated, most severe status kept, photos deduplicated). Automatic save BEFORE so you can undo. A "📥 imported" chip on the merged team cards. The QR code route was tested then dropped — scanning after WhatsApp compression was too fragile on dense codes. ⚠️ Like everything: keep a physical compass and a paper map. The phone can fail. The 🚨 is a coordination aid, NOT a substitute for preparation.

🌍 State 3 — EXTERNAL RESCUE BRIEFING (OSM View × Rescue Mode) — coordination with external rescue services (firefighters, GRIMP, SDIS).

🚪New built-in tag Map entry point (category "🚨 Rescue" in the legend) to mark the main emergency entries 📍Surface GPS per team: "📍 Surface GPS" field in the team card (format "lat, lng" WGS84), for the rescue command post / firefighter meeting point 🌍🌍 OSM View button available in the Edit banner AND in the 3 Live footers → show the map's position on OpenStreetMap without leaving the active view 🚒Dedicated firefighter briefing PDF (🚒 button): an A4 page with clickable OSM + Google Maps links + teams + surface GPS + critical POIs (map entry / emergency exit / quarry accesses) 📤A "Surface briefing" page automatically integrated into the post-mission PDF report

💾 Save Offline — Offline OSM View — a 💾 Save Offline button available in the OSM View modal and in the home's OSM View widget. One click downloads the OpenStreetMap tiles covering the map's area and stores them in the phone's local storage (200 tiles max per click, to respect OSM's usage policy — click the button again if you want to extend coverage or do several zoom levels). Once cached, the 💾 icon stays visible to tell you the area is saved, and the OSM View opens directly off-network (underground, no-signal area, airplane mode) — no error message, no connection attempt: the app detects there is cache and displays the map instantly. The cache is shared between the home OSM View, the OSM View modal and Rescue Mode — a single Save Offline covers all three. Field reflex: Save Offline before you leave, while you still have a signal.

🌍 OSM mode (widget's ⛶ button) — the OSM map goes big. A search bar (in the title line, also available on the collapsed widget) searches your georeferenced maps and their points — 100% local, live results. You can stack several maps (➕) and manage everything in the ≡ "Plans & filters" modal: ▲▼ order (images AND paths), per-map opacity, global display switches, aggregated tag filter, and 5 per-map filters (🖼️📍🛣️🌐🏛️). Data layers shipped hidden by default in a ZIP are displayed too (they used to be invisible with no way to enable them) — filter them like the others via the category chips or the tags.

📉 The sheet states the depth. When the plan’s levels carry one, “-2” becomes “-2 · -35 m” — in the text summary, in the PDF and on the scenario cards. A level number is an internal coordinate; a depth tells you how much rope and which team.
aide.sec.vue-osm.titre: 🌍 OSM view — your survey on a real map
aide.sec.vue-osm.html:
🌍Projects a georeferenced plan onto OpenStreetMap: you see where your galleries actually run under the ground. Two places — the home preview and full screen from an open plan📏Measure — distance and area, by clicking on the map. ⚠️ A measurement taken here is more reliable than in plan mode: it depends on no calibration, the coordinates are already geographic🎯Surface coordinates — one click gives you the latitude and longitude right above the chosen point, with a copy button. That is what you hand to a team coming in from above🗂️Several plans at once — order, opacity and per-plan filters. And one click on a label shows every plan carrying it (“Gironde”…), a second click removes them🎨The colours you chose in ≡ Legend apply here too, and each plan in the stack keeps its own📝Your session work shows up — points, paths, zones and structures you added, even if they are not in the plan yet📐Alignment quality of your links — both ends of a portal designate the same place: the distance between them once projected measures your georeferencing directly. Sorted worst first

⚠️ Accuracy comes from YOUR alignment, not from the map. The coordinates read are exact for the point on the map; “right above that gallery” depends on the georeferencing of the plan carrying it. A badly aligned plan moves its galleries, not OpenStreetMap. That is exactly what the alignment gap measures for you.

🔒 The only screen that reaches the internet. The OSM view downloads map tiles from OpenStreetMap — nothing else leaves, none of your data. It is on by default: you can turn it off in ⚙️ Configuration → 🗺️ OSM View (OpenStreetMap); strict offline mode and incognito also disable it. The 💾 button pre-loads tiles so you can use it without a network. Only georeferenced plans appear here.
aide.sec.mesure.html:
📐Distance measurement — click to place points, total shown at bottom-left ⬛Area measurement — 📏/⬛ toggle in the group, draw a polygon, the app computes the area in m² (auto ha beyond 10,000 m²) 📏Total length of paths — sub-action of the Paths group, floating panel with filters by type 🗺️Route — the shortest path between 2 or more points following the existing roads

📏 Total length: opens a small bottom-right panel with 3 checkboxes (Main / Secondary / Path). The total length of the checked paths is shown in meters, and the included segments are highlighted in magenta on the map. Also includes the roads of visible data layers. Not exported in the PNG image legend.

🗺️ Route: add waypoints (click on the map, search by name/id/tag, or the 🧭 My position button which takes your current tracker position), the app computes the shortest path using the existing roads (session + data layers, even hidden layers — useful if the roads are drawn directly onto the PNG and you want to gain performance). The bottom-left label shows the distance, the ⏱️ estimated time and the active speed mode (🤕 Injured 2 km/h / 🐌 Slow 3 km/h / 🚶 Normal 5 km/h default / 🏃 Fast 7 km/h, + 15 min of pause per intermediate point). The mode is changed via a selector in the route modal and is kept across sessions. The route appears in neon cyan with a distance label at bottom-left. On re-click, the modal opens in navigation mode: ⏮️ Start, ⏭️ End, 🔁 Full loop buttons, and 🎯 per waypoint to center the map on it.

🔄 Living route: every position recalibration (map click, "📍 I am here", portal arrival) recalculates the active route from your new position (remaining stops kept in planned order, avoidances respected). "📍 I am here" on a point that is a route stop = passage validation (green ✓ marker, struck-through line in the modal, stop excluded from future calculations) — in any order. All stops validated → "🎉 Route complete", the path clears (the tracker trail stays). Validations survive reloads (saved with the session).

🚫 Avoidance constraints: ⛔ Inaccessible Zone (Zones group) = a hard constraint, the route will never pass through it, never relaxed. 🚫 Avoidance preferences (collapsible section in the route modal) = a soft constraint: points to avoid (search / ID / map click) + tags to avoid + margin (px, default 100). If there is no alternative path, the app computes it anyway by passing nearby and shows an orange message ⚠️ Unable to avoid: X, Y. Preferences remembered locally per map.

📉 Depth and elevation profile. If your plan’s levels carry a depth (entered in the Generator or in the levels menu), a route gives you its elevation profile: altitude along the way, metres climbed and descended, highest and lowest points. 🕳 And a shaft is no longer counted as a flat line: its length now includes the height between the two floors. ⚠️ Only when both levels have a depth — otherwise the old calculation applies and your existing plans do not change.
aide.sec.edition-points.html:
✏️Enable add mode — direct click on the ✏️ icon → ON/OFF toggle. In ON, each click on the map places a new point. 📸Photos attached to the point (max 5) — section in the add/edit modal. 📷 Take / 🖼️ Gallery buttons ✏️Edit an existing point — blue button in the marker's popup (reopens the same pre-filled modal) 📌Reposition a misplaced point — 📌 Reposition button in the popup: your next click on the map moves the point there (banner at the top of the map, with Cancel). The point keeps its name, type, description, photos and level — only its position changes. Undoable with Ctrl+Z. Only on your points: a data-layer point must first be opened for editing from 🔍 Filters. 🌐GPS coords in the popup — if the map is georeferenced, a point's popup automatically shows the GPS coordinates (lat/lng WGS84) computed right after the description, with a 📋 button to copy to the clipboard. Active for all points (session AND data layers). 🗑️Delete a point — click the marker → popup → 🗑️ Delete this point button. To undo an accidental deletion: Ctrl+Z.

📸 POI photos: attach up to 5 photos per point (mobile camera via 📷 or gallery import via 🖼️). Auto JPEG q85 compression max 1920px. 100% local on this device — never sent over the Internet. 44×44 thumbnails in the marker's popup (tap → full-screen viewer with pinch-zoom + pan + horizontal swipe to navigate between photos). Included in all exports (session ZIP + map generator ZIP) + restored automatically on re-import. A 5th 📸 counter in the header + a section in the "📊 Session details" modal.

🫧 A point's popup (tap a marker): 📍 I am here recalibrates tracking on that point (it is also what confirms your position for the emergency exit) · 🧭 Go there computes a route from your position · ➕ Route adds the point as a route step · ☆ Favorite · 🔊 Read the note aloud · 📋 copyable GPS coordinates if the map is georeferenced · 📸 photo thumbnails · 🌀 badge of inter-map links. On your own points only: ✏️ Edit, 📌 Reposition (then tap the map) and 🗑️ Delete, undoable with ⏪.
aide.sec.structures.html:
🟡1st-mass pillar (polygon, yellow fill) 🟠2nd-mass pillar (polygon, orange fill) — auto-tagged level -1 in M-LVL 🔵Wall (polygon, blue fill) 🟨1st-mass quarry face (polyline, yellow stroke) — this is a LINE, not a closed polygon 🟧2nd-mass quarry face (polyline, orange stroke) — auto-tagged level -1 in M-LVL 🧹Erase (last point / last in-progress OR closed structure / 🎯 selection by map click / all) 🗑️🗑️ Delete — red button in the structure's popup, under “Convert”. No confirmation: Ctrl+Z undoes it.

Mapping the underground architecture: load-bearing pillars (1st/2nd mass of limestone), retaining walls, and quarry faces. For polygons (pillars + walls), place at least 3 points then re-click the lit icon to close. For polylines (faces), place at least 2 points then re-click the icon to validate the line. No pathfinder effect (read-only — that's different from the ⛔ Inaccessible zone which blocks the route).

🔄 A quarry face that is really a gallery. This is the common case with an imported survey: everything lands as structures, while some vectors are galleries. But routing only runs on paths — a survey entirely made of structures does not have “a poor route”, it has none. The Convert button on the card reclassifies the vector and brings it into the calculation. ⚠️ Session objects only: for a layer shipped in the plan, open it for editing first (🔍 Filters).
aide.sec.traces.html:
🟩Draw a main road 🟪Draw a secondary road 🟨Draw a path 🪜Inter-level junction (dashed magenta) — sub-action visible only if multi-level mode is enabled. A bridge between 2 levels for the pathfinder. 📏Total length of paths (floating panel with filters by type) 🧹Erase (last point, last path or all) 🗑️🗑️ Delete — red button in the path's popup, under “Convert”. No confirmation: Ctrl+Z undoes it.

🔄 Changing an object’s type. On a path’s card, a Convert button turns it into another type — including a quarry face. Geometry, level and note are kept. ⚠️ An open vector can only become a path or a quarry face; it will never become a zone, because that would mean closing the geometry — inventing data nobody surveyed. ⚠️ Only works on objects in your session: for an object shipped inside the plan, open its layer for editing first (🔍 Filters).
aide.sec.zones.html:
⬛Draw a fill zone 🟥Draw a collapse zone 🟦Draw a water zone ⛔Draw an inaccessible zone (red/black hatching) — blocks the pathfinder ✅Close the current zone (at least 3 points) 🧹Erase (last point, last zone or all) 🗑️🗑️ Delete — red button in the zone's popup, under “Convert”. No confirmation: Ctrl+Z undoes it.

Place at least 3 points then re-click the 1st point to close the zone, or use the ✅ button.

🔄 Changing a zone’s type. A zone’s card carries a Convert button: it can become another zone, or a pillar / wall. Geometry, level and note kept. ⚠️ A closed vector will never become a path — that would mean opening it. ⚠️ Session objects only (for an object from the plan: bring its layer in from 🔍 Filters).
aide.sec.optimiser-plan.html:
A light map = fast loading, smooth navigation, less risk of a mobile memory crash. Main tips:

🖼️Base image ≤ 8,000 px per side, JPEG quality 85 format (5-10× lighter than PNG) 🗂️Just 1 image layer ideally — merge legends/markers into the base PNG 🛣️Many roads? Draw them in the PNG + hide the JSON layer. The pathfinder uses the roads even when hidden 📍Dense points? Split them into several toggleable layers (shafts / passages / electrical…) ⚡Perf mode: 🎯 Balanced on a modern mobile, ⚡ Performance on an old device

More details and precise figures in the Documentation 📖 (📚 Help / Docs group), "Optimize your map for performance" section.
aide.sec.code-acces.html:
🔐Optional locking of the app at every startup 🤳Face ID / Touch ID / Windows Hello biometrics if the device supports it (native WebAuthn) 🚫5 wrong codes in a row = temporary lock (10 min, then 1 h, 6 h, 24 h with each new run); the app unlocks by itself when the delay ends. No code recovery if forgotten.

To be enabled from the home page only: ⚙️ Configuration → 🔐 Local access code → "🔐 Enable the access code" button. Enter a 4-6 digit PIN, confirm, then accept the biometrics if offered. On the next startup, the app will ask for your code before opening.

⚠️ Important note: this is a usage barrier, NOT data encryption. Photos and sessions remain in clear text in the browser's local storage. The PIN is hashed client-side (SHA-256 + random salt) and never sent over the Internet. Write down your code carefully — no recovery is possible if forgotten (no backend, no email reset). On lockout: the only solutions = reinstall the app (loss of session + non-saved maps) OR contact the author (who won't be able to do anything, consistent with the no-backend philosophy).
aide.sec.astuces.html:
Exclusive modes: Measurement, Add point, Recalibration and Paths are mutually exclusive — enabling one automatically disables the others.

Active mode: as long as a mode is active, its group stays open to allow direct access to the secondary actions (erasing the last point, for example).

Changing icon: the group's main icon reflects the active mode (for example 🟩 on the Paths button when a main path is in progress, or 📍 on the Tracker during recalibration).

🛡️ A window cancels the active tool: opening a modal (Settings, Filters, Documentation, Rescue Mode…) during a measurement, an edit, a path, a zone, a structure or a recalibration disarms the mode — no more ghost clicks after closing. The tracker is never cancelled, and the form of the point you just placed does not interrupt editing.
aide.sec.depannage.html:
📡 App stuck after a soft update (loader with no CSS, page frozen, assets badly loaded): the most frequent cause is an edge CDN serving corrupted content (wrong MIME, truncated asset, etc.). First reflex: disable your VPN, change network (4G ↔ Wi-Fi), and retry. The GitHub Pages CDN sometimes has rotten regional edges — switching IP/geo zone is often enough to unstick it.

🆘 Emergency kill switch: if the app stays stuck even after changing network, open https://<domain>/?killsw=1 in a private tab (Chrome/Safari, NOT the PWA) — this resets the app cache + empties all the app's technical files without touching your data (maps, sessions, photos, prefs preserved). Then reload normally.

🆘 Manual reset via dedicated page: if the URL param isn't enough (HTML cache stuck), navigate to https://<domain>/killsw.html — a standalone 100% inline page (CSS+JS), zero dependencies, works even if the rest of the app is broken. Three steps shown: app cache reset, technical files purged, ready to reload.

🔄 Optimized soft update: the ⚙️ Configuration → 🔄 Force the update flow is designed to be 10× faster (from ~45s-3min to ~3-10s depending on network). The app downloads the update in the background during the purge; on reload, the current cache is preserved, without downloading twice.

⚠️ These tools delete NO user data (maps, sessions, photos, prefs, backups). They only purge the cache of the app's files (HTML / CSS / JS / icons). When in doubt, 📤 Export the profile BEFORE so you have a complete backup at hand.
aide.sec.liaisons-inter-plan.html:
Link a point on one plan to a point on another plan — like a portal between two touching networks (two neighboring quarries, overview plan ↔ detail plan).

Create: click a point (session or data layer) → button 🌀 Link to another plan → pick the target plan then search the arrival point (name, id or tag — no need to open the other plan). The link is bidirectional: visible in both points' popups. A point can carry several links.

Use: in the point's popup, 🌀 line → ➜ button → confirmation → the app switches plan (session saved automatically), switches to the arrival point's level and drops you on it (blue flash). Visual marking is your choice: give the point the "Portal" tag for its dedicated vortex icon, or keep any tag (no marking). 📍 Recalibration on arrival: physically crossing a portal (a link's ➜, a route's "Take the portal") recalibrates your tracker position onto the arrival point — multi-plan search and the manager do not (viewing ≠ moving).

↩️ Back: after a jump, a floating "Back: <plan>" button (15 s, bottom of screen) brings you back to the plan and the exact view you came from (level + zoom). Jumps stack — 3 chained portals = 3 possible returns. Discreet when needed: [–] shrinks it to a ↩️ mini-chip (click = re-expand), [✕] closes it — your choice is remembered for future jumps. 🔎 Multi-plan search: search a point across your whole library from the search bar at the top of the home screen (centered in the header — confirm with Enter or 🔎) or via the Ctrl+K search ("Search across all plans" button) — one click loads the right plan and centers on it.

🌀 My links: on the home screen, lists all your links (⛔ if a plan is missing, ➜ to go there, 🗑️ to delete). 🕸️ Graph view: toggle 📋 List ⇄ 🕸️ Graph — the library as a network (plans = bubbles with badges + counter, portals = lines whose thickness follows the number of links, unlinked plans in a dedicated strip). Click a bubble = open the plan, click a line = border detail, bubbles draggable.

🧭 Inter-plan route: request a route to a point on another plan (Route modal → "🌐 Destination on another plan", or 🧭 button in the multi-plan search). The app compares portals at real cost, shows the steps and total distance — your modal waypoints are visited first, in order. "🗺️ Let's go" draws the route and lets you walk: the crossing is offered when you are AT the portal (floating "🌀 Next portal" button, the popup's ➜, or "📍 I am here" on the portal point). Check "🌀 Route across multiple plans" in the multi-plan search to cross intermediate plans (A → B → C, 3 crossings max) — each arrival draws that leg and offers the next portal. Impossible? The message tells you why (no portal, plan offline, destination cut off…).

Target plan missing from this device → the link still shows (⛔) but "going there" requires adding the plan. Deleting a point also deletes its links (both sides). Links travel with the session export. If a tag filter hides the arrival point, a warning is shown (the filter is never modified). Plan data unreachable (offline) → the app says so instead of a silent "0 points".

📐 Alignment gap. Each link can show a distance in metres — this is not a distance to walk. A portal's two ends mark the same physical spot seen from two plans: properly georeferenced, they should land at the same point on the world map. The gap measures how far they miss by, hence how good your alignment is — smaller is better. It only appears if both plans are georeferenced; otherwise nothing is shown (writing “0” would suggest a perfect alignment). No colour coding, deliberately: 20 m is huge in a small quarry and negligible across a 5 km network. In full-screen OSM View (🎚️ Filters → 🌀) the same measurement becomes a list sorted worst first, and a click frames both ends. An absurd gap almost always comes from one of the two plans' georeferencing, not from the link.
aide.sec.carnet.titre: 📔 My logbook — the history of your trips
aide.sec.carnet.html:
Auto-save keeps the current state of a plan; the logbook keeps the history. Every exploration becomes an archived trip: date, time actually spent in the app, distance travelled with the tracker, points / paths / zones added, photos taken, the path you walked, and a free-form note you can write even weeks later. Clearing a session does not delete trips already filed.

Where: the 📔 My logbook button on the home screen (no plan to load) · from a plan: Session modal → 📔 Trip in progress. When: archived automatically when you leave the plan, or 🏁 Close my trip to file it right away — a new one starts immediately.

🚶 Field trip or 🖥️ desk work? The logbook tells them apart on its own: if you moved it is a trip — and a single "📍 I am here" is enough, even with the tracker off. If you only annotated without moving it is desk work, filed in a collapsed section of its own. Totals count field trips only. A session is kept if 50 m were travelled OR if you worked 10 min with at least 1 annotation (below that, nothing is kept). To fix the classification: the 🚶 / 🖥️ buttons on the logbook sheet, or straight from a map in the Session modal → 📔 section. The fix is final.

📏 Distance without the pedometer — if you walk without the tracker and drop "📍 I am here" markers along the way, the app links them to estimate your distance, following the galleries rather than the straight line. You start at A, pass through C, reach B → A→C then C→B are counted. The figure is always flagged as estimated ("600 m of it estimated"): it never passes itself off as a measurement. If the pedometer measured between two markers, the pedometer wins. A map click to correct yourself and a portal crossing do not count as travel.

🧭 Refine track — during the trip the app counts in a straight line so that "I am here" stays instant underground; the gallery-following pass runs once, when the trip is filed (which is why your distance goes up then). The 🧭 Refine track button in the Session modal runs it whenever you like: it recomputes the distance and redraws the route between your markers. ⚠️ That redrawn route is a reconstruction: the app assumes the shortest path, so a detour or a U-turn will not show up. It appears in the trip sheet only — your GPX/KMZ exports and the heatmap keep the actually recorded track.

📖 Stories tab: the free note and the PDF of Story mode were locked inside a plan's screen — you had to load the quarry to re-read your own notes. They are now listed here across all plans, with the note rendered as Markdown and editable right there (same note, not a copy). A PDF shipped inside the plan's ZIP still requires the plan to be loaded.

The logbook starts empty: earlier trips were never recorded. Everything stays local (nothing is uploaded); each trip can be deleted from its sheet; beyond 500 trips the oldest ones are removed. Photos are not copied (the logbook points at yours — a deleted photo shows 🚫). The logbook is included in the profile export: switching devices carries your outing history with it.

📔 Start an outing by hand. In 📊 Session details, when nothing is running, the “📔 Start an outing” button opens one right away on this map — even if “Keep a logbook of my outings” is unticked in ⚙️ Settings. Unticked, the app no longer opens anything by itself: this is the only way to record an outing, and it closes normally (🏁 Close, or on a map change) without a next one starting. If an outing is already running, the button gives way to 🏁 Close.

⚙️ Where the logbook is set. The “📔 Keep a logbook of my outings” checkbox lives in ⚙️ Configuration on the home screen → 🔒 Privacy & security. It applies to all your maps. From a map, its state is shown in ⚙️ Settings → “🏠 Set from the home screen”.
profileio.sec_histpdf_hint: PDF documents attached to your maps (📖 Stories tab). ⚠️ Very heavy: up to 100 MB per map. Unchecked by default — without them, a re-imported profile arrives with the free notes but no documents.
osm_home.portails.label: Portals
osm_home.portails.hint: Links both ends of each inter-plan connection. The gap shown measures georeferencing quality: both points mark the same real place, they should overlap.
ipl.mgr.ecartTitre: Distance between this link's two ends, projected through each plan's georeferencing. They mark the same spot: the smaller the figure, the better the alignment.
osm_home.portails.qualiteVide: No measurable link: BOTH plans of a portal must be displayed and georeferenced.
osm_home.session.label: Session
osm_home.session.hint: Also shows work in progress (points, tracks, zones, structures) saved in each plan's session, on top of what the plan itself contains.
osm_home.session.badge: Current session — not in the plan yet
gen.sig.l93Converti: File detected as Lambert 93 (EPSG:2154): {n} coordinates were converted to latitude/longitude. Check that the position on the map matches your site before continuing.
gen.sig.hAuto: Computed automatically to match the terrain proportions — otherwise the plan overflows the canvas.
gen.sig.couleursNiveauHint: Creates a distinct legend type for each level, with its own colour. Without this, every level comes out in the same shade and they blend together. You can rename and recolour each entry afterwards in ≡ Legend.
gen.sig.beaucoupFeatures: Large file: {n} objects. The import accepts them, but displaying the plan may be heavy on mobile. If the map struggles, re-import with fewer layers.
gen.sig.canvasAlerteIos: Background of {mpx} million pixels. Above roughly 16, an iPhone may show an empty background (Safari limit). No issue on PC or Android. If the plan is meant for iPhone, a width of about {conseil} px stays under the limit.
gen.sig.canvasAlerteRam: Background of {mpx} million pixels — that is a lot. Generation may fail for lack of memory (the app holds two images that size at once), and the background will be empty on iPhone. You can try: if it does not complete, go back down to about {conseil} px wide.
gen.sig.legendeEdite: {n} legend customisation(s) — they will be embedded in the generated plan.

gen.tiff.errInjection: Image decoded but could not be injected into the form: {err}
tiff.err.pasUnTiff: this file is not a TIFF
tiff.err.bigTiff: BigTIFF not read — re-export as a classic TIFF from QGIS
tiff.err.tuile: tiled image not read — re-export as strips (untick “tiled” in QGIS)
tiff.err.compression: compression not read — re-export as LZW, Deflate or uncompressed
tiff.err.bits: bit depth not read — 8 bits per channel required
tiff.err.canaux: channel count not read — 1 (grey), 3 (RGB) or 4 (RGBA) required
tiff.err.photometrie: colour type not read (palette, CMYK or YCbCr) — re-export as RGB
tiff.err.rgbIncoherent: inconsistent file: RGB declared with fewer than 3 channels
tiff.err.bandesAbsentes: no image data in the file
tiff.err.lzwTropLong: LZW stream inconsistent with the declared dimensions
tiff.err.deflateIndispo: Deflate decompression unavailable in this browser
tiff.err.pasDeCalage: no georeferencing in the file — this is a plain TIFF, not a GeoTIFF
tiff.err.rotation: the georeferencing contains a rotation — re-export the plan north-up
tiff.err.crsInconnu: coordinate system not supported — re-export in Lambert 93, Web Mercator or WGS84
tiff.err.calageHorsTerre: the georeferencing places the plan off Earth — check the coordinate system
